But cities have to deal with managing the growing diversity of data, applications and devices needed to develop services, and to tailor these services to each citizen's requirements. The establishment of human-centered computing methodologies for developing services leads cities towards the Open Innovation, meant as the key to develop innovative ecosystems characterized by real-life experiments that result in new services. PEOPLE project represents a step towards this evolution by putting in practice the concept of human-centred computing in real scenarios (Livings Labs), where citizens participate continuously and actively in the creation and validation of new tailored services. The outcomes of implementing the methodology proposed by PEOPLE develop, implement and deploy innovative services based on ICT infrastructures with guidelines set by citizens, covering users' real needs sustained by collaborative basis.
Notes: The study concerns citizen-centered smart-city service development and open innovation; OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment is not investigated.

Author: L. Zhang; Y. He; H. Wu; N. D. Hatziargyriou
Title: An Optimal Scheduling Framework for Integrated Energy Systems Using Deep Reinforcement Learning and Deep Learning Prediction Models
Abstract Note: Model-free deep reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising method for addressing the scheduling challenges in integrated energy systems. However, uncertainty in system states continues to hinder optimization efforts. This paper proposes a hybrid framework that integrates deep learning prediction models with deep reinforcement learning scheduling models. Initially, Gaussian process regression is employed to extract interval information from stochastic variables, organizing the input data into structured time series segments. Subsequently, a hybrid prediction model, combining Transformer and long short-term memory networks, is constructed for multi-step interval prediction of these stochastic variables. Finally, a synchronized training mechanism couples the twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient method with the hybrid prediction model, fully exploiting trends in system state changes to enhance scheduling performance. Experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework using open-source data to analyze the influence of different prediction methods on scheduling. Results show that the proposed approach improves overall performance by 22.4% compared to the baseline method.
Notes: The study concerns energy-system scheduling using open-source data; it does not investigate OSS projects or any abandonment-related lifecycle concept.

Author: Y. Tanoto; A. Bruce; I. MacGill; N. Haghdadi
Title: Impact of High Variable Renewable Penetrations on Dynamic Operating Reserves in Future Indonesian Electricity Industry Scenarios
Abstract Note: This paper investigates the impact of high variable renewable energy (VRE) penetrations on dynamic operating reserves, focusing on the future of Indonesia's Java-Bali grid. We use an open source evolutionary programming-based techno-economic optimization model, National Electricity Market Optimizer (NEMO), to first assesses possible least cost generation mixes both with and without VRE, and under different carbon pricing scenarios and reserves requirements. While low cost generation, major deployment of wind and solar still requires high levels of conventional dispatchable plant, typically thermal and hydro, and while there are costs associated with this overhead, it does have interesting implications for operating reserves. Our study explores this issue and shows that not only might wind and solar reduce overall industry costs for Java-Bali in 2030, the resulting generation mix would have significantly higher reserves, and hence ability to cover unexpected plant failures and other interruptions, over most of the periods with considerably high demand.
Notes: The study concerns electricity-grid generation planning and operating reserves; open-source software is only the optimization tool, with no OSS lifecycle or maintenance topic studied.

Author: D. Rainer; D. Hoffmann
Title: AutomationML Library Space: A concept for sharing and versioning Engineering Data Models
Abstract Note: The digital transformation in engineering requires standardized information models to close gaps in digital value chains and to increase engineering efficiency. Despite the existence of several digital data models for engineering, their reuse is hindered by a lack of robust, guided mechanisms for sustainable development and publication. While the IT sector widely leverages Git-based workflows for sharing and collaborative software development, engineering data modelers have yet to adopt similar practices effectively. Our requirements and gap analysis reveals that, while services like Microsoft GitHub offers a robust starting point for collaborative and efficient modeling, more specialized mechanisms are required to effectively adapt Git-like workflows to the unique needs of engineering models. In response, we propose a novel method and an implementation that combines the capabilities of GitHub’s open-source collaboration strengths with engineering-specific enhancements as versioning and flexible deployment across both open and closed platforms. Interested readers are invited to explore and test the presented solution.
Notes: The study proposes Git-like sharing and versioning for engineering data models; OSS is a collaboration platform or implementation context, with no investigation of OSS project lifecycle or abandonment.

Author: Q. Zhang; Y. Gong; C. Yang; G. Geng; Q. Jiang; X. Li; Q. Fang
Title: Insecure Operating Scenario Synthesis for RES-Integrated Power System: A Physics-Pattern Constrained Generative Learning Approach
Abstract Note: Synthesizing diverse and more severe insecure operating scenarios (OSs) is essential for power system equipment capacity expansion planning, control strategy formulation and operational risk awareness. However, with the increasing penetration of renewable energy, existing methods struggle to account for complex physical feasibility and source-load pattern distribution. In this paper, a physics-pattern constrained generative learning approach is proposed to synthesize more severe N-1 insecure OSs, thereby augmenting the scarce data in practical applications. Firstly, a deep clustering network is employed to learn embedded feature of base insecure OSs in clustering-friendly spaces and assign patterns to base OSs. Subsequently, a classification network is trained in embedded feature spaces to infer the pattern of specific OS, thereby transforming the prior patterns into learnable loss that guides the synthesis of OSs with specific pattern. Finally, a reparameterized generative network incorporating physical feasibility and pattern consistency constraints is proposed to synthesize the N-1 insecure OSs via differentiable sampling. Case studies on the State Grid 126- bus system and a practical 861- bus system demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms benchmarks in terms of the validity and pattern consistency of synthetic OSs, and the synthesized OSs are verified to facilitate the deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm in learning more robust N-1 corrective control strategies.
Notes: The study concerns power-system operating scenarios and control strategies, not OSS projects or repositories.

Author: Y. Li; J. Yang; W. Dong; C. -K. Wen; S. Jin
Title: CSI-Based Instantaneous Rainfall Monitoring in Sub-6 GHz for ISAC Applications
Abstract Note: Rainfall is a critical environmental variable with significant societal and economic impacts, yet conventional monitoring systems suffer from limited spatial granularity and high deployment cost. Leveraging existing cellular networks offers a promising opportunity for continuous and ubiquitous rainfall monitoring. Opportunistic rainfall sensing using microwave links above 10 GHz has been extensively investigated. However, most large-scale cellular networks still operate in the sub-6 GHz band. In this frequency range, rainfall estimation based only on received signal strength is inherently limited and is usually restricted to coarse rain detection or rainfall-level classification. To address this challenge, this work presents a channel state information (CSI)-based measurement campaign and spatiotemporal analysis of natural rainfall at 3 GHz, together with the release of an open-source dataset. The results show that the delay spread generally increases with rainfall intensity, whereas the decay factor and Rician  $K$ -factor generally decrease as rainfall intensifies; however, these delay-domain metrics may exhibit non-monotonic behavior under severe rainfall. The angular spread generally increases with rainfall intensity, while antenna correlation shows a non-monotonic trend, initially decreasing and then increasing with rainfall intensity. Building on these observations, we propose CSI-Transformer RainNet, a CSI-based rainfall regression model for sub-6 GHz cellular links, which jointly exploits spatiotemporal channel features for instantaneous rainfall estimation. The proposed model shows strong temporal robustness. It achieves consistent performance on test datasets collected 10–40 days after training, using only three CSI measurements sampled at 3-second intervals. Each CSI measurement is extracted from a single orthogonal frequency division multiplexing symbol. Under the same experimental conditions, CSI-Transformer RainNet achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of  $2.24~\mathrm {mm/h}$ , outperforming the commercial Doppler weather radar, which has an RMSE of  $2.51~\mathrm {mm/h}$ . These results highlight the potential of communication-based rainfall monitoring as a low-cost and scalable complement to conventional meteorological sensing systems.
Notes: The study uses cellular-network measurements and releases an open-source dataset, but its subject is rainfall sensing and estimation, not OSS project lifecycle or maintenance.

Author: S. Abreo; J. D. Espinoza; C. A. Fajardo
Title: A Latin American Institution’s Journey in Digital Systems Education: From Breadboards to FPGA and RISC-V Design
Abstract Note: This paper presents the evolution of digital systems education at the Universidad Industrial de Santander, beginning with hands-on projects using discrete logic chips on breadboards. The curriculum progressively adopted hardware description languages (VHDL and Verilog) and eventually integrated RISC-V open hardware through the RVfpga project. This transformation has positioned the university as a regional reference in Latin America and contributed to the professional success of its graduates in the global semiconductor industry. The paper describes key milestones, methodological decisions, and pedagogical strategies that enabled this shift, analyzes its impact on student engagement and learning outcomes, and offers recommendations for institutions seeking to modernize their digital systems curricula. The experience illustrates how sustained curricular innovation and project-based learning can foster academic excellence and real-world impact in electronics and computer engineering.
Notes: The study concerns digital systems education and adoption of RISC-V open hardware, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: S. H. Jihan; A. Segev
Title: Humanitarian Assistance Ontology for Emergency Disaster Response
Abstract Note: Massive amounts of open data related to a crisis aren't fully used to identify humanitarian needs because most of the data exists in an unstructured format, thus hindering machines in its interpretation. Automatic processing of crisis data in a short time period would provide useful information to decision makers. To address these problems, this article presents a method for merging ontologies and logic rules to represent humanitarian needs and recommend appropriate humanitarian responses. The main advantage of the method is that it identifies humanitarian needs and prioritizes humanitarian responses automatically, including health survival issues and possible responses by creating a working system during the evolution of the crisis. The method is implemented on 125 real data reports from the Hurricane Wilma crisis and compared to the actual support provided.
Notes: The study analyzes humanitarian crisis reports and response recommendations, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: K. Gama
Title: Civic apps competitions: Preliminary findings on the longevity and quality of their outcomes
Abstract Note: Competitions became a common ground for city halls fostering the creation of useful mobile and Web applications for Smart Cities. A fact that started to be pointed out is that many of the apps developed in these civic apps competitions tend to be abandoned after the winners are announced. Different authors attempt to explain that phenomenon by arguing in different directions, alleging bad features, bad quality or lack investments from the cities organizing the contests, among other reasons. Evidence in academic research is mostly based on superficial research about the contests and interviews with organizers of these competitions. We wanted to gather quantitative data to measure the longevity of apps that eventually become abandoned, their perceived quality and the impact of the civic apps produced in these contests. In a case study of contests held by three big metropolitan cities in different countries, we surveyed a total of 122 apps that won prizes in 11 civic apps, from 2009 to 2015. We also interviewed organizers of the events to combine their perspective with our results. After checking app by app, we gathered information on which ones are still being used and estimated the impact based on different parameters such as the number of users, and the economic impact of those. This article presents preliminary findings of this study.
Notes: The study examines civic apps produced in city competitions, not OSS/FLOSS projects or repositories.

Author: W. Wang; N. Niu; M. Alenazi; L. Da Xu
Title: In-Place Traceability for Automated Production Systems: A Survey of PLC and SysML Tools
Abstract Note: Automated production systems are critical enablers for Industry 4.0 because these design-to-order, custom-built mechatronic systems are not only capable of delivering automation capabilities to satisfy the stakeholder requirements in the manufacturing/production domain, but doing so for a long period of time (e.g., several decades) during which numerous changing needs shall also be accounted for. Although traceability has long been recognized as key to sustain changes, little is known about how the traceability information is managed in place, i.e., in the native environments where the engineering artifacts reside. We contribute in this paper a survey of traceability support within state-of-the-practice tools: seven for programming logic controllers and six for building models in systems modeling language. We draw the similarities and differences from our survey results, and further present a design by leveraging the in-place traceability to better support the development and evolution of automated production systems.
Notes: The study concerns industrial automation systems and PLC/SysML tools, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: S. Santhi; M. Murugan; T. Srinivasan; S. KG
Title: Corn Leaf Disease Detection using Deep Learning Techniques
Abstract Note: The agricultural productivity is the major sector of Indian economy. The rate of misdiagnosis is extremely high, and conventional approaches for identifying crop diseases are ineffective in terms of both time and money. Accurate disease diagnosis also improves economic loss and decreases the effectiveness of agricultural output. The deep neural networks technology have shown promising results in the early phases of machine learning, allowing experimenter for increasing the precision in detection of object and identification systems. The major goal of experiment was to locate and classify maize leaf diseases using appropriate deep-learning-based architectures. This proposed work employ the known dataset of the Corn leaf infection dataset, open source, in trials where this carried work must discriminate between unhealthy and diseased leaves as this exploration where specific areas of the leaf are affected. This proposed work employed block model of VGG for identifying classification problem, kept the most possible number of parameters to be low for achieving rapid convergence while maintaining good accuracy. To locate the contaminated area in the maize leaf, this constructed model applied the cutting-edge deep learning model VGG 16. To show the effectiveness of our suggested solution, this experiment runs on several end-to-end tests and analyses the results. The outcomes demonstrate that the proposed model performs rather existing method given the available data. The proposed model achieves mean average detection precision of55.30% and a classification accuracy of 95.25%.
Notes: The study concerns maize leaf disease detection; “open source” describes the dataset, not an OSS project or ecosystem.

Author: Y. Guo; C. Seaman; N. Zazworka; F. Shull
Title: Domain-specific tailoring of code smells: an empirical study
Abstract Note: Code smells refer to commonly occurring patterns in source code that indicate poor programming practices or code decay. Detecting code smells helps developers find design problems that can cause trouble in future maintenance. Detection rules for code smells, based on software metrics, have been proposed, but they do not take domain-specific characteristics into consideration. In this study we investigate whether such generic heuristics can be tailored to include domain-specific factors. Input into these domain-specific heuristics comes from an iterative empirical field study in a software maintenance project. The results yield valuable insight into code smell detection.
Notes: The study evaluates domain-specific tailoring of code-smell detection heuristics; it does not study software decay or its consequences, and the record does not establish an OSS lifecycle focus.

Author: A. González; C. R. García; S. Candela
Title: Providing learning computing laboratories using hosting and virtualization technologies
Abstract Note: This paper presents a computing hosting system to provide virtual computing laboratories for learning activities is presented. This system has a distributed structure and it is based on clustering, hosting and virtualization technologies. All the components used in its development are free software tools. The computing lab model provided by the system is a more sustainable and scalable alternative than the traditional academic computing lab, and it requires lower costs of installation and operation.
Notes: The study presents a virtual computing laboratory for learning; free software is used as a tool, and sustainability refers to the lab model rather than OSS project lifecycle.

Author: X. Jiang
Title: Technological Narrative Structure of Cloud Teaching Research Community: A Grounded Theory Study Based on County High School Assistance
Abstract Note: In the context of digital transformation in education, Cloud Teaching Research (CTR) is regarded as a key pathway to overcoming the dilemmas of county high school education and achieving the sharing of high-quality resources. However, existing studies predominantly focus on the functional empowerment of technology, rarely delving into the micro-power dynamics and the reshaping of teacher subjectivity induced by technological embedding. To address this gap, based on a typical case of county high school assistance, this study adopts the Grounded Theory method to construct a "Technological Narrative Structure Model of Cloud Teaching Research Community" through in-depth interviews and participant observations with 30 frontline teachers and administrators. The findings indicate that: (1) The embedding of CTR technology features significant "asymmetrical technological power", where its "panoptic" surveillance and elite cultural capital trigger survival anxiety among county teachers. (2) To cope with this pressure, the teacher group develops a "dual narrative strategy": engaging in "performative collusion" (e.g., data brushing) on the "front stage" to meet assessment requirements, while practicing "implicit resistance" on the "back stage" through private mutual aid to dissolve hegemony. (3) Through continuous negotiation, "localization reconstruction" and virtual emotional connection eventually lead the community from fragmentation to "identity awakening and regeneration". The conclusion suggests that the key to empowering the revitalization of county high schools lies in transcending the logic of "digital surveillance" and shifting towards "professional service" and the activation of "local wisdom". This study recommends reshaping technological ethics, legitimizing localization adaptation, and building collaborative mechanisms based on emotional connections.
Notes: The study concerns a cloud-teaching community in county high schools, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: R. Bajaj; G. Bathla; A. Gupta; Anurag; L. Pawar
Title: Optimized Ensemble Model for Wholesale Market Prediction using Machine Learning
Abstract Note: Wholesale is the practice of selling low-cost items to retailers or directly to customers. The wholesale customer dataset primarily provides information on customers' interest in the wholesale market and their annual consumption of a specific product. The goal of this research is to create a preferred machine learning model that can assist wholesale retailers in increasing their production and profit by anticipating the quantity of products necessary in the market. The proposed research study has initially attempted to incorporate typical machine learning models, but it has not resulted in satisfactory results, so this research study has further progressed to propose an ensemble model, and the satisfactory results were obtained for the proposed model. The algorithms utilized in developing this model are SMOreg and Kstar. SMOreg is a programming problem-solving algorithm, which is utilized for training the support vector machine (SVM). The proposed dataset was collected from the UCI Machine Learning repository, which is an open-source platform.
Notes: The study concerns wholesale-market prediction using a customer dataset; the UCI repository is only the data source, not an OSS project population.

Author: Y. MEKOUAR; I. SALEH; M. KARIM
Title: Integration of Data Acquisition and Modeling for Ecological Simulation of CO2 Emissions in Urban Traffic: The Case of the City of Paris
Abstract Note: Considering the environmental protection requirements, our study proposes a modelling of CO2 emissions in the city of Paris. At the core of our approach, we have developed a model based on probabilistic algorithmic equations to estimate CO2 emissions on a street-by-street basis. Our model relies on a data preprocessing process that includes significant steps of cleaning and imputation, which are essential to ensure data integrity and reliability. These data, sourced from various APIs, cover road traffic, weather conditions, and air quality. This work is crucial to refine the model and ensure the accuracy of the results. The main objective of our research is to develop dynamic models and simulations that accurately reflect real-time CO2 emission rates for each street in Paris. We have developed a modelling method that combines environmental and urban factors to faithfully represent road traffic emissions in Paris. Consequently, our results demonstrate the potential to simulate CO2 emissions, highlighting emission patterns that vary according to the time of day and atmospheric conditions and showing the influence of environmental factors on urban emissions. From a technical standpoint, the equations we created are based on a hybrid CNN-LSTM model [1] and contribute to continuous development and refinement through deep learning. This approach aims to create a reliable and robust predictive tool for simulating CO2 emissions from road traffic. By doing so, we contribute to sustainable urban planning and reduce the environmental impact of road traffic through efficient management and real-time emissions monitoring.
Notes: The study population is urban road traffic and CO₂ emissions in Paris, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: Z. Ma; Y. Deng; Z. Qiao; Q. Zhang; C. Zhou; F. Wu; Y. Zhang; J. Ren
Title: A Fine-Tuning Data Recovery Attack on Generative Language Models via Backdooring
Abstract Note: Generative language models (GLMs) are increasingly integrated into modern intelligent applications to power intelligent functionalities. Developers often fine-tune open-source GLMs on proprietary data and deploy them in real-world applications. In this paper, we reveal a novel model supply chain attack that exploits this workflow: by injecting backdoors into the source code of an open-source GLM, an adversary can induce the model to memorize fine-tuning data and later regenerate it via crafted prompts. We propose Lure, a new backdoor-based data recovery attack that exploits memorization capabilities of fine-tuned models. During fine-tuning, Lure stealthily injects unique and attacker-enumerable hash prompts, and incorporates a Position-Decay Weighted Aligned Cross-Entropy Loss into the original fine-tuning loss, strengthening the association between injected prompts and corresponding data samples for effective data recovery. To achieve stealthy and transparent attack injection, Lure employs a stealthy backdoor within the model’s source code, enabling automatic injection of hash prompts during fine-tuning and thus maintaining the user’s original fine-tuning workflow. Lure also proposes several optimizations to maintain minimal impact on the performance of the original task and external training state. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the remarkable efficacy of Lure, achieving a 45%-68% data recovery rate while maintaining the attack’s transparency, stealthiness, and showcasing its ability to evade existing defenses.
Notes: The study examines a backdoor attack and data recovery in fine-tuned language models, not OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment; open-source models are the attack setting.

Author: Dominique Davison; Ashley Z. Hand
Title: SMART CITY ARCHITECTURE AND PLANNING
Abstract Note: It is essential to consider data at all scales: the human, the building, and the urban levels to truly adapt how architects design buildings of the future to be part of a holistic, sustainable urban system. With a growing emphasis on life cycle analysis or assessments at the building level, design decisions are often evaluated by the up‐front impact of manufacturing through the full use of the material or component as a way to understand the impact of building design and to assess sustainability. Several measures have been created‐such as the US Green Building Council (USGBC) and Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) program‐to help architects and building owners evaluate their buildings. The Internet of Things (IoT) or Internet of everything: the communication of a broad array of sensors in the built environment creates new opportunity for architectural design that will create truly smarter buildings and better, more sustainable and resilient cities.
Notes: The record concerns architectural design, buildings, and smart cities, with no OSS project or ecosystem population.

Author: Hsin-Hsi Tsai; Yi-Ta Chuang; Chih-Wei Yi; Yi-Chang Wang
Title: A study on wearable electrocardiograph
Abstract Note: The emergence of wearable devices based on advances in MEMS and low-energy technologies makes low-cost sustained physiological monitoring possible and brings health care into a new territory. But until now, most wearable devices for physiological monitoring do not have FDA approval and the measured data may have some level of noise. In this work, to understand the feasibility of applying wearable electrocardiograph for heart activity monitoring during jogging, we propose a jogging monitoring system based on wearable devices and provide some experimental results. First, the proposed jogging monitoring system is sketched. Next, the traditional ECG tests and the fundamental ECG morphology are introduced. And then, a QRS detection algorithm is introduced and implemented to process ECG data. Last, we collect ECG data by a wearable device in jogging, and some MLII lead ECG records from the MIT-BIH database are selected for comparison. The accuracy of the implemented QRS detection algorithm against both data sets is provided.
Notes: The study concerns wearable ECG monitoring and signal-processing data, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: M. Emmanuel; R. Rayudu
Title: Equipment loading and voltage unbalance in the distribution network with distributed PVs
Abstract Note: One of the value attributes of photovoltaic distributed generation (PV-DG) is the offset of feeder currents which in turn reduces the overall feeder loading. In addition, for remote nodes at the end of the distribution network with high voltage unbalance tendency, PV-DG can be used to reduce this unbalance factor and its associated adverse impacts. This paper discusses the impact of distributed PVs on the equipment loading and voltage unbalance factor of the distribution network. Impact analysis has been carried out on the IEEE-13 distribution bus at different penetration levels using the Open-source Distribution System Simulator (OpenDSS). The results showed that for such highly loaded distribution network, PV-DG can be used to offset feeder current, active power demand, equipment loading and voltage unbalance. In addition, we use typical localized average temperature, solar irradiance and load demand profiles in this interconnection study.
Notes: The study analyzes photovoltaic impacts on distribution-network loading and voltage balance; OpenDSS is only the simulation tool, with no OSS lifecycle or maintenance topic.

Author: B. Heiles; N. Blanken; A. Kuliesh; M. Versluis; K. Jain; G. Lajoinie; D. Maresca
Title: PROTEUS: A Physically Realistic Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound Simulator—Part II: Imaging Applications
Abstract Note: The development of new imaging paradigms in the field of contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) is hindered by the difficulty to control complex experimental variables in a laboratory setting, such as vascular geometries, nonlinear ultrasound wave propagation in tissue, or microbubble positions within vessels as a function of time. This development would greatly benefit from the ability to control and reproduce independently these conditions in a simulated environment. Here, we report a physically realistic CEUS simulator, PROTEUS, that generates synthetic contrast-enhanced radio frequency (RF) data. In this article, we show that PROTEUS enables flexible investigations of imaging parameters on CEUS, including innovative transducer architecture, such as row-column addressed arrays, microbubble size distribution, pulse sequences, and vascular geometry. We demonstrate how PROTEUS can emulate various 2-D and 3-D imaging modes, such as pulse inversion (PI) or amplitude modulation (AM), echo particle image velocimetry (PIV), or ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM). Finally, in an investigative simulation case study, we evaluate the impact of microbubble size distribution on ULM on a simulated set of 15000 frames. It is released as an open-source tool for the scientific community.
Notes: The study develops and evaluates an open-source ultrasound imaging simulator; it does not investigate the simulator project's maintenance, activity, or lifecycle.

Author: A. M. Riesco; M. A. Artaso; M. Belandia; S. Pickin
Title: Still in the first steps of a barefoot knowledge engineering
Abstract Note: This paper reviews and offers some reflections on the current state and potential of expert systems (ESs) for human and sustainable development (HSD) in the context of developing countries (DCs). We propose a framework for the evaluation of ES development projects, and assess some significant recent applications drawn from three areas of relevance for HSD: health care, agriculture and water resource management. In the light of the foregoing we draw some conclusions and suggest some preliminary methodological guidelines to address the objective of a “barefoot” knowledge engineering for “appropriate” ESs, i.e., ESs that indeed meet HSD objectives in the context of DCs.
Notes: The study reviews expert systems for human and sustainable development in developing countries, with no OSS project lifecycle or abandonment-related focus.

Author: C. Capodiferro; M. Mazzei
Title: Applications of deep learning and artificial intelligence methods to smart edge devices and stereo cameras
Abstract Note: The aim of this work is to test a computer vision application that, thanks to edge computing and the use of devices optimised for artificial intelligence, allows the distance of objects from a fixed point to be measured. The distance is calculated between two or more points of interest with a certain accuracy and within a certain range. The point of interest from which to measure the distance is determined by a fixed point or an object recognised through deep learning techniques, with which the neural chip can perform very efficiently and with low energy consumption. In this work we used an Edge AI device with stereo cameras, a Luxonis OAK-D, equipped with an Intel Myriad-X neural chip and an improved version of the open-source Luxonis DepthAI library. The application is very complex and has the potential to be used in a variety of areas where precise positioning and real-time object recognition is required. The areas of applicability can be diverse, including assisted navigation, spatial data analysis, robotics, surveillance, health and safety, construction and engineering, surveying and mapping, transport, sports and fitness.
Notes: The study evaluates a computer-vision application using an open-source library; it does not investigate OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: R. M. Kshirsagar; S. M. Kherde; S. R. Dharmadhikari
Title: Investigation of 3D Printed Lithophane Quality Improvement on A FDM Printer
Abstract Note: In recent years, the process of creating lithophanes has involved the use of 3D printing technologies to produce transparent plates of varying thicknesses and when backlit, these lithophanes create images. The process includes building a 3D model of the lithophane with open-source 3D modeling software. Then, the print parameters are chosen, and white PLA filament is used for printing. This research investigates the optimization of 3D-printed lithophanes on Fused Deposition Modeling (FDM). Using Taguchi’s DOE approach, five key parameters such as brightness, contrast, maximum thickness, minimum thickness, and vector per pixel were chosen, and each was investigated at three distinct levels. A total of 27 samples were systematically designed and printed to examine the impact of these parameters on the quality of 3D-printed lithophanes. The Python script was used to analyze the experimental data and find the best set of parameters to enhance the lithophanes’ visual appeal. The results of this investigation provide significant contributions to the field of 3D printing, particularly with regard to the production of visually engaging and captivating lithophane prints through the use of FDM technology.
Notes: The study optimizes 3D-printed lithophane quality; open-source modeling software is only a tool, with no OSS lifecycle or abandonment topic.

Author: G. Wikle; F. Wang
Title: An Hourly-Scale Adaptation of the KSTS Algorithm for Synthesizing Extreme Weather Scenarios
Abstract Note: As the power grid decarbonizes, electricity is increasingly produced by solar and wind power plants with the support of energy storage facilities, which smooth out weather-driven production variability and intermittency. Decarbonization removes firm generation capacity such as coal power plants and methane-powered thermal plants. The decline in firm generation capacity will require system operators to mitigate extended renewable droughts to guarantee resource adequacy and system reliability. In practical operation, it is not uncommon to experience lack of wind energy or solar irradiance to sustain renewable resource energy production. Planning for renewable droughts generally relies on stochastic modeling of wind and solar production on an hour-by-hour basis to include hourly renewable variability and intermittency. This work extends a proof-of-concept stochastic weather and renewables production simulation algorithm. The resulting hourly synthetic solar and wind production profiles can be used in resource adequacy simulations to verify that proposed generation portfolios will meet system reliability standards during a variety of weather scenarios. The source code is published as an open-source project.
Notes: The study develops a simulation algorithm for power-grid resource adequacy; open-source code is only the implementation context, with no OSS lifecycle or abandonment-related topic.

Author: R. Kalapatapu; K. Bitra
Title: Low-Cost AI Agents for Cybersecurity and Data Governance in Small-Scale Manufacturing Industries
Abstract Note: Small-scale manufacturing industries are increasingly adopting digital technologies to improve productivity and operational efficiency, but they often face significant challenges in implementing robust cybersecurity and data governance due to limited financial resources, technical expertise, and IT infrastructure. Traditional enterprise security solutions are frequently expensive and difficult to maintain, making them unsuitable for small and medium-sized manufacturing environments. This paper proposes a low-cost Artificial Intelligence (AI) agent-based framework for cybersecurity and data governance that provides intelligent, automated, and scalable protection against cyber threats while ensuring secure data management. The proposed framework integrates lightweight AI agents capable of continuous network monitoring, anomaly detection, malware identification, phishing detection, access control, and compliance monitoring. Machine learning algorithms analyse system logs, network traffic, and user activities to identify suspicious behaviour in real time, while data governance modules enforce data classification, integrity verification, privacy preservation, and secure access policies. By leveraging open-source AI models and cost-effective cloud-edge deployment, the framework minimises implementation costs without compromising security performance. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the proposed system achieves a threat detection accuracy of 95.8%, precision of 95.2%, recall of 94.9%, and an F1-score of 95.0%, while significantly reducing response time and operational overhead compared with conventional rule-based security approaches. The results indicate that low-cost AI agents can provide an affordable, efficient, and adaptive cybersecurity solution for resource-constrained manufacturing industries. The proposed framework supports secure digital transformation, enhances regulatory compliance, protects critical manufacturing data, and improves the resilience of small-scale industries against evolving cyber threats.
Notes: The study evaluates cybersecurity and data governance for manufacturing; open-source AI models are only a technology used, with no OSS project lifecycle or abandonment-related subject.

Author: K. Kalaiselvi; A. Kh; S. VR
Title: Assessing the Impact of COVID-19 on Inflation Dynamics in India: A Machine Learning Approach
Abstract Note: This research work aims to study COVID-19's impact on the Indian economic system. The Consumer Price Index of India for different commodities from January 2013 to March 2023 is used for the dataset. The paper implements modern tools like Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) methods to analyse the impact COVID-19 had on the inflation rate in the economic state of India. This paper uses Linear regression, K-nearest neighbors, random RandomForest Regression, Gradient Boosting Regressor, and one deep learning LSTM model to analyse the Consumer Price Index dataset and the Unemployment Rate dataset from multiple open-source databases. During the study, comprehensive evaluation was done to calculate the model's performance with parameters like r2_score, Mean Square Error (MSE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and (MAE) mean absolute error to forecast the CPI, and Inflation rate using the best performing model which was found to be the RandomForest Regression with the r2_score of 0.990665. : We could see a sharp increase in both the inflation rate and consumer price index in 2020 at around 6.62% as expected and by using the best-performing model with an r2_score of 0.99 the forecasting is visualized. This paper analyses and forecasts the inflation rate and CPI of India by implementing Machine learning methods adding new information to the already existing COVID data analysis.
Notes: The study forecasts Indian inflation using CPI and unemployment data; open-source databases are only data sources, with no OSS project lifecycle or maintenance topic.

Author: R. -I. Toma; E. -A. Sinoi
Title: Large-Scale Bankruptcy Risk Prediction for Romanian SMEs Using Robust Machine Learning Approaches
Abstract Note: Predicting corporate bankruptcy is vital for financial stability and risk management. This paper presents a large-scale, open data study on bankruptcy risk prediction for Romanian small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), leveraging a unique dataset of over 4 million company-year financial statements from 2019 to 2023. Our robust data pipeline addresses real-world challenges such as noise, missing values, and the prevalence of “atypical” (inactive, shell, or chronically distressed) companies, through systematic cleaning, outlier removal, and targeted exclusion from the healthy class. We construct and compare two modeling datasets: one using raw accounting indicators and another based on engineered financial ratios, both linked with multi-year company histories. We benchmark classical machine learning models (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression) and deep learning architectures (LSTM, GRU) on these variants. Our results show that tree-based ensemble ML models perform best on raw accounting data with multi-year sequences, achieving AUC-ROC > 94.00%, while deep learning models achieve their highest precision and F1-score when trained on engineered financial ratios. Excluding atypical companies substantially improves model precision and minority class recall. These findings highlight the importance of careful dataset design, robust data curation, and multi-year context for effective largescale bankruptcy prediction. Our work establishes best practices and actionable insights for credit risk assessment in emerging economies.
Notes: The study population is Romanian SMEs and their financial statements, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: Y. Zhao; Y. K. Zhao; C. Wan; Y. C. Lin
Title: 3D-Carbon: An Analytical Carbon Modeling Tool for 3D and 2.5D Integrated Circuits
Abstract Note: Environmental sustainability is crucial for Integrated Circuits (ICs) across their lifecycle, particularly in manufacturing and use. Meanwhile, ICs using 3D/2.5D integration technologies have emerged as promising solutions to meet the growing demands for computational power. However, there is a distinct lack of carbon modeling tools for 3D/2.5D ICs. Addressing this, we propose 3D-Carbon, an analytical carbon modeling tool designed to quantify the carbon emissions of 3D/2.5D ICs throughout their life cycle. 3D-Carbon factors in both potential savings and overheads from advanced integration technologies, considering practical deployment constraints like bandwidth. We validate 3D-Carbon’s accuracy against established baselines and illustrate its utility through case studies in autonomous vehicles. We believe that 3D-Carbon lays the initial foundation for future innovations in developing environmentally sustainable 3D/2.5D ICs. Our open-source code is available at https://github.com/UMN-ZhaoLab/3D-Carbon.
Notes: The study develops a carbon-modeling tool for integrated circuits; open-source code is only the tool’s availability context, with no OSS project lifecycle topic.

Author: H. Heidarabadi; M. Graner; H. Hesse
Title: BattProDeep: A Deep Learning-Based Tool for Probabilistic Battery Aging Prediction
Abstract Note: Profitability, reliability, and efficiency of battery systems across a broad spectrum of applications, including both stationary energy storage and automobile sectors, are critically dependent on accurate battery lifespan predictions. Traditional deterministic models for estimating battery longevity are inadequate, as they do not fully capture the complex and stochastic nature of battery degradation. In this contribution BattProDeep is introduced as a groundbreaking tool that employs a deep learning-based framework to offer probabilistic predictions of battery aging, thereby addressing the uncertainties according to the experimental dataset. BattProDeep sets itself apart with its innovative features. It adopts an open-source approach, enhancing transparency and fostering collaboration across the global research community. This not only enriches the tool with a diverse range of insights but also accelerates advancements in the field. Utilizing cutting-edge TensorFlow and TensorFlow probability libraries, BattProDeep offers a data-driven method for battery aging prediction, improving accuracy and applicability across different battery types and conditions. Furthermore, its probabilistic predictions include confidence intervals, providing crucial information about prediction uncertainty, which is invaluable for risk management and decision-making in critical sectors. The validation results show that the mean prediction error for our approach stays within ±0.2 % for high-cyclic applications, with all true measured capacity loss values falling within the 95 % confidence interval, affirming its reliability for risk management. These qualities, coupled with the benchmarking of BattProDeep according to the literature, make BattProDeep a key instrument for advancing battery health management, leading to more dependable and sustainable battery-powered solutions.
Notes: The study develops an open-source battery-aging prediction tool; OSS is the tool’s distribution approach, not the subject of project abandonment or lifecycle-related factors.

Author: S. Sivarajeswari; S. P. Ranjana; E. Swathi; S. Kandasami
Title: Smart Sewage Sentinel
Abstract Note: Particularly in large cities, sewage systems play an important role. Smart cities are emerging quickly, but the issues people encounter still stem from the prehistoric era. The inhalation of hazardous gases found in the manhole is a major cause of the continued deaths of sewage employees. The multivariable, nonlinear, time-varying, and random treatment process characteristics of the sewage system contribute to its instability and unpredictability. Modern developments and sophistication in planning are greatly needed in the modern environment. Hence, this project proposes a smart sewage monitoring system based on IOT for Smart City. This project is constructed on the open-source Arduino electrical platform. The system uses multiple components of a Gas sensor, ESP32 Camera, Servo motor, DC motor, Robotic gripper, Motor Driver, and a node MCU. A battery is used in this system to store the electricity generated by photovoltaic panels. A DC motor is used to convert electrical energy into mechanical motion. Additionally, it can control speed and direction. Gas sensors are installed to avoid manhole explosions by maintaining proper underground gas concentration by detecting the presence of inflammable gases. A robotic gripper is a mechanical device designed to grasp and manipulate objects. It is used to perform tasks that involve picking up, moving, and releasing objects. Servo motors offer precise control in robotics. The ESP32 camera integrates Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and image processing. Gas sensors monitor gas purity. Blynk App alerts the IoT system of issues and updates user data on a cloud-based platform.
Notes: Open-source Arduino is only the platform for a smart sewage-monitoring system; the study does not examine OSS project lifecycle or maintenance.

Author: C. R. García; A. Quesada; S. Candela; E. Carrasco; A. González
Title: Using a virtual and hosted lab for information systems technologies
Abstract Note: This paper describes how to provide suitable computing systems for information systems technologies learning using virtualization and hosting technologies. The main functionalities and components of a university learning lab based on these technologies are presented. All the software components used in its development are open source. Also, the use of this lab, providing the computing systems required for the learning activities of different matters related to the information systems technologies, is illustrated. The model of computing lab proposed is a more sustainable and scalable alternative than the traditional academic computing lab.

Author: M. Salomon; E. Koshchenko; A. Sergeyuk; R. Holmes; G. C. Murphy; T. Fritz
Title: From Disruptions to Discussions: How GenAI Impacts Human Interactions in Software Development
Abstract Note: New technologies often change how an individual performs work, such as how generative AI (GenAI) can help a developer write code. New technologies can also impact how people interact with one another, such as how GenAI’s ability to summarize API documentation can reduce the need for developers to ask each other technical questions. In this paper, we report on a two-phase mixed-method study exploring how GenAI influences how humans interact in software development. During phase one, 30 industrial software developers provided data over a period of 5 to 12 days as they worked, contributing 627 experience sampling responses and 207 end-of-workday survey responses. To gain further insight into their work, we interviewed 22 of these developers. During phase two, 131 additional professional developers responded to a survey to explore whether and how the results from phase one are seen across a larger population. Our analysis of the data found that (1) the ability of GenAI to help answer low-level technical questions in a timely way enables developers to see GenAI as a technical mentor, providing opportunities for developers to turn to tools rather than teammates; (2) developers perceive that GenAI can help them experience more focus and experience fewer flow disruptions; (3) GenAI can help developers pursue more meaningful conversations with their colleagues by shifting human interaction towards clarification, joint reasoning, and exploring alternative perspectives; and (4) in the presence of GenAI, developers report still seeking human-to-human interaction for contextual expertise, mentorship, and social connection. Together, these findings show what changes, when it changes, and what teams can do next in response to this shift in team interaction dynamics, where GenAI increasingly handles routine technical queries and human conversations center on context, reasoning, and connection. Teams can adopt norms for delegating questions, sustain human judgment in complex decisions, and create space for expertise, mentorship, and connection, alongside increasing technical self-sufficiency.
Notes: The study explicitly examines industrial and professional software developers and their interactions with GenAI, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: C. P. Pavan Kumar Hota; V. B. Polinati; P. Gottumukkala; S. P. Kumar Gudla; S. Murali Krishnamachari; P. Neelima
Title: Intelligent Automation in Equity Research: A LangChain–FAISS–LLM Framework for Financial News Understanding and Insight Generation
Abstract Note: Today, equity research is heavily reliant on the analysis of large amounts of unstructured financial data, such as news reports, earnings releases, and market updates. Traditional approaches are frequently slow, inconsistent, and influenced by human judgment, necessitating greater automation. This study introduces a financial news analysis tool built with modern Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods and tools such as LangChain, FAISS, and Streamlit, as well as Large Language Models. Initially based on OpenAI's GPT models, the tool later shifted to open-source models from Hugging Face to reduce costs and improve scalability. Semantic search with vector embeddings, automatic summarization, and a simple interface for financial queries are among the key features. FAISS allows for quick and relevant information retrieval, whereas LangChain improves response accuracy through effective prompt management. Testing revealed that the system was capable of producing results in milliseconds while extracting financial insights with greater than 80% accuracy. This work presents a practical, efficient, and cost-effective solution for using AI in equity research, providing better support for financial decision-making.
Notes: The study develops a financial-news analysis tool; open-source models are only an implementation choice, with no OSS project lifecycle or abandonment topic.

Author: A. Osa-Sanchez; B. Garcia-Zapirain
Title: Real-Time Air Quality Monitoring: A Smart IoT System Using Low-Cost Sensors and 3-D Printing
Abstract Note: This project developed a portable air quality station housed in a 3D-printed enclosure, designed to streamline data sampling and minimize material use in laboratory settings. With health concerns related to specific gases and particulates, especially for vulnerable populations such as asthmatics and children, this innovation has significant potential for improving public health. The importance of indoor ventilation has been underscored by COVID-19, which is primarily transmitted through airborne particles, highlighting the need for efficient monitoring and risk reduction strategies. The station utilizes open-source Python software, with a Raspberry Pi as the core data collection and storage unit, interfacing with various sensors via GPIO, serial, and I2C connections. The modular design of the device allows users to customize measurements and focus on specific pollutants. Validation through end-user testing confirmed the system’s effectiveness and usability in practical settings. The portable setup offers a cost-effective solution for building air quality networks that address the needs of vulnerable groups. The module demonstrated a high reliability rate of 95.30% in detecting common pollutants, validated through CO2 monitoring in classrooms (with a 90.47% reliability compared to commercial devices) and outdoor air quality assessments (with an 85.63% reliability rate.
Notes: Open-source Python is used as a tool for an air-quality monitoring system; the study does not examine OSS project lifecycle or maintenance.

Author: A. D. Suleiman; Y. Tang; D. Hou
Title: Factors Impacting Faculty Adoption of Project-Based Learning in Computing Education: A Survey
Abstract Note: This research full paper investigates the factors influencing computing educators' adoption of project-based learning (PjBL) in software engineering and computing curricula. Recognized as a student-centered pedagogical approach, PjBL has the potential to enhance student motivation, engagement, critical thinking, collaboration, and problem-solving skills. Despite these benefits, faculty adoption remains inconsistent due to challenges such as insufficient institutional support, time constraints, limited training opportunities, designing or sourcing projects, and aligning them with course objectives. This research explores these barriers and investigates the strategies and resources that facilitate a successful adoption. Using a mixed-methods approach, data from 80 computing faculty were collected through an online survey comprising closed-ended questions to quantify barriers, enablers, and resource needs, along with an open-ended question to gather qualitative insights. Quantitative data were analyzed using statistical methods, while qualitative responses underwent thematic analysis. Results reveal that while PjBL is widely valued, its adoption is often selective and impacted by challenges in planning and managing the learning process, designing suitable projects, and a lack of institutional support, such as time, funding, and teaching assistants. Faculty are more likely to adopt or sustain PjBL when they have access to peer collaboration, professional development, and institutional incentives. In addition, sourcing projects from research, industry partnerships, and borrowing from peers emerged as key facilitators for new projects. These findings underscore the need for systemic support structures to empower faculty to experiment with and scale PjBL practices.
Notes: The study examines faculty adoption of a teaching approach in computing education, not OSS project lifecycle or abandonment-related concepts.

Author: G. Sánchez; L. Wei; V. Hagenmeyer
Title: LaserTag: A Tool for Autonomous XAI-Guided Physical Adversarial Perturbations in Industrial Vision Pipelines
Abstract Note: We introduce LaserTag, an open-source toolchain for studying physical-world adversarial effects on industrial vision pipelines. The system couples lightweight classifiers with XAI methods and a reproducible pan–tilt laser actuation rig to identify salient image regions and probe them with controlled optical perturbations. Designed for dependability research, it supports interactive operation, automated logging, and repeatable experimentation. We evaluate LaserTag on three representative industrial controllers, highlighting practical vulnerabilities in vision-based status recognition. Rather than optimizing attacks, the toolchain provides an auditable testbed for autonomous XAI-guided targeting, surrogate-model transferability analysis, and countermeasure assessment. Experiments show that XAI-guided laser perturbations reliably induce both failure masking and spurious alarms, while several digital defenses—including color-channel suppression, highlight clipping, and laser inpainting—successfully restore correct predictions across both main and surrogate models. Code and models are released for reproducible research.
Notes: The study evaluates adversarial effects and defenses in industrial vision pipelines; open source describes the toolchain, not an OSS project lifecycle or abandonment-related topic.

Author: Z. Wang; H. Yang; Y. Li; Q. Yao; T. Yu; C. Zhang; W. Liu; W. Lin; J. Zhang; Y. Liu; M. Cheriet
Title: Co-Route Fiber Recognition and Status Diagnosis Based on Integrated Sensing and Communication in 6G Transport Networks
Abstract Note: The 6G transport network facilitates the Internet of Everything (IoE), carrying numerous services and emphasizing the paramount importance of its reliability. However, within the transport network, the issue of co-route fibers arises. The co-route fibers, encompassing both co-cable and co-trench fibers, presents a significant latent hazard for service disruptions, posing a substantial threat to the seamless connectivity envisioned for the 6G era of pervasive IoE. The segregation of communication and sensing in the transmission network results in mutual interference between communication and sensing signals, rendering it difficult to promptly address sudden fiber interruptions. This article proposes an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) architecture within transport networks, aiming at the online discernment of co-cable fibers, characterization of fiber optic trenches, and real-time classification of fiber vibration events. In the domain of co-cable fiber identification, our approach has successfully reduced the nuisance alarm rate to an impressive 5.3%, while simultaneously elevating the recognition accuracy to an outstanding 99.7%. As for co-trench fiber identification, our proposed methodology not only facilitates the discernment of co-trench fibers but also achieves an impressive accuracy of 97.7% in classifying fiber trenches. Moreover, in the realm of fiber state prediction, our solution has achieved a remarkable recognition accuracy of 98% across six distinct vibration events. These results underscore the robust performance of the proposed ISAC architecture, which will effectively safeguard the survivability of 6G IoE.
Notes: The study concerns 6G transport-network fibers and service reliability, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: X. Zhang; L. Cheng; K. Ni; X. Yang; X. Wang; J. Duan
Title: Exploring the Influencing Factors of College Students' AI Dependence in Course Assignments: A Grounded Theory Study
Abstract Note: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence has significantly reshaped college students' approaches to completing course assignments, giving rise to increasing dependence on AI tools. However, the mechanisms underlying this dependence remain insufficiently explored. Adopting a grounded theory approach, this study investigates the influencing factors and formation mechanisms of AI dependence among undergraduate students. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 36 undergraduates from a comprehensive university in eastern China, and the data were systematically analyzed through open, axial, and selective coding. The findings reveal that students' AI dependence is driven by a “motivation-maintenance” mechanism. Perceived usefulness, including efficiency enhancement and quality optimization, functions as the initial trigger, while a stress-avoidance schema-manifested in low self-confidence, fear of failure, and peer pressure-plays a central role in sustaining dependent behaviors. These factors interact with course task design and institutional environments to reinforce habitual AI use. This study conceptualizes AI dependence as a contextualized adaptive process within higher education and provides implications for assessment design, academic support, and responsible AI integration.
Notes: The study population is undergraduate students and their dependence on AI tools, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: A. Bisenbaev; B. Nurzhauabev; N. Nyssanov; D. Zhankulov; M. Raikhan; A. Bektaev
Title: Transfer Learning for Landmark Recognition and Geographic Localization in Smart City Environments
Abstract Note: Geographic localization of pictures is becoming more useful in smart cities, in digital forensics investigations, and open-source intelligence collections. The given paper demonstrates a modular system of visual geolocation that was developed and tested on an actual urban area and is based on transfer learning with EfficientNetV2-M. The system works through three supplementary modules: (1) a closed-set landmark classifier with test accuracy of 97.0 percent in 14 classes using a two-phase fine-tuning protocol; (2) a district-level coordinate regression model with a mean Haversine error of 312-445 meters; and (3) an open-set building retrieval model using FAISS approximate nearest-neighbor search over dense visual embeddings. To test the prototype, data was taken to build the prototype and then test it using the data of a modern planned capital city with a unique modern skyline (Astana). The whole training and deployment process was run on a single local GPU and was not dependent on any external mapping services. Findings indicate that geographic specialization achieves accuracy several orders of magnitude higher than the global geolocation baselines in the target city.
Notes: The study develops and evaluates a visual geolocation system for smart-city images; OSS is mentioned only as an intelligence context, with no OSS project lifecycle or maintenance topic.

Author: D. A. S; B. S; G. D; U. N
Title: VulnCloud Scanner: Lightweight Multiengine Scanning for Container Security
Abstract Note: Container security has become a major issue for organizations adopting cloud-native architectures. Existing scanner reports lack exploit context, deployment-specific applicability and knowledge of whether the vulnerable function is ever executed. This leaves security teams overwhelmed by alerts that are theoretically flagged but practically irrelevant. This paper presents VulnCloud, an open-source Kubernetesnative framework that turns inconsistent scanner results into actionable and deployment-aware risk signals. The VulnCloud orchestrates many scanning engines through a confidenceweighted consensus model. Enriches findings with exploitlikelihood and threat intel, context-aware applicability filtering, and validates exploitability through hybrid static call-graph and runtime reachability analysis. An admission controller enforces the composite risk score through policy-as-code to block images. On evaluation over 100 diverse container images, VulnCloud achieves a decision accuracy of 96.8 %, a precision of 99.7 %, and a false-positive rate of 0.5 %. This offers security teams a fully auditable, CI/CD native pipeline that is low-noise and highassurance.
Notes: The study evaluates container vulnerability scanning and security enforcement; open source describes the framework, not an OSS project lifecycle or maintenance concern.

Author: G. Chen; M. Tong; J. Yin; M. Wang; J. Cao; H. Wang
Title: SecureGraphFL: A Privacy-Preserving and Attack-Resilient Federated Learning Framework for Traffic Prediction
Abstract Note: Traffic prediction is a critical research topic with significant transportation management and planning implications. graph neural networks (GNNs) have gained widespread use in traffic prediction due to their ability to capture relationships between different traffic sensors effectively. However, traditional centralized learning approaches struggle to meet the increasing demand for user data privacy. While federated learning (FL) addresses these privacy concerns, it introduces new challenges, particularly when one or more clients are compromised by malicious attacks or single-point failures, leading to significant degradation in global model performance. To address these issues, we propose SecureGraphFL, a FL framework based on graph convolutional networks (GCNs) and actor–critic networks that ensures security while maintaining high predictive accuracy. SecureGraphFL introduces three key innovations: 1) incorporating a parallel speed difference prediction task to enhance prediction performance; 2) utilizing a cosine similarity-based graph construction method to more effectively capture patterns from similar traffic sensors; and 3) designing an actor–critic network-based client selection mechanism to exclude malicious clients, ensuring the stability of the global model. Experiments on two open-source datasets, PEMS-D7 and METR-LA, demonstrate that in the absence of malicious or failed clients, SecureGraphFL matches state-of-the-art centralized methods and significantly outperforms traditional FL algorithms like FedAVG and FedATT. Moreover, in scenarios involving malicious clients, our client selection mechanism effectively mitigates their impact, maintaining performance levels comparable to those without any malicious activity. The code for this article is available at: https://github.com/cry-C/SecureGraphFL.
Notes: The study develops a federated-learning framework for traffic prediction; open-source datasets and code are resources, not the subject of OSS project lifecycle or maintenance.

Author: V. Jethose; A. R. Venodhani; P. Balaji; A. S. Priya; K. Chaturveda Sree; T. Gowarthanan
Title: Air Pollution Forecasting with Machine Learning: A Step Toward Proactive Environmental Management
Abstract Note: Urban air pollution is still a critical environmental and public health issue, fueled by increasing levels of fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5), Ozone (O3), and Sulfur Dioxide (SO2). Current monitoring systems, though accurate in real-time measurement, are inadequate in predicting pollutant levels, which prevents proactive decision-making. This project suggests a data-driven solution based on Multitask Learning (MTL) to forecast hourly concentrations of major air pollutants up to 24 hours ahead. Building on past meteorological observations and pollution records, we compare the performance of a variety of algorithms—Random Forest, Extra Trees, Lasso Regression, and Support Vector Machines—in the MTL setting. To provide temporal consistency in the predictions, we add regularization methods like temporal smoothness penalties. Model training and model performance measurement are done on an open-source urban air quality dataset, and the metrics used are Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and R-squared (R2). The MTL architecture facilitates the concurrent forecasting of different pollutants and, thus, reduces computational time and enhances inter-pollutant correlation capture. This study offers a replicable method for short-term air quality forecasting, with relevance to urban planning, emergency management, and environmental policy. The findings show the potential for the application of machine learning in air quality management as a scalable instrument for cities that seek to reduce pollution-related health hazards.
Notes: The study uses an open-source air-quality dataset to forecast pollution; it does not examine OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: H. Chauhan; A. Vishvkarma; B. Singh; N. Kumar; R. Verma; S. Negi
Title: AI-Driven Employee Attrition Prediction and Workforce Retention Analytics using Explainable Machine Learning
Abstract Note: One of the debated topics under Organizational productivity & employee retention is Employee Attrition and how it can pave the way for a sustainable business solution. Simplified relationships between a few human resource practices, and employee turnover actually exist as well, and bring little conviction to why the strategies will work. Create A-Driven Employee Attrition Prediction and Workforce Retention Analytics Framework from the open-source data set IBM HR Analytics Employee Attrition Dataset. We have also proposed a method for training and translating a model in order to maintain uniformity and clarity in predicting employee attrition while improving overall performance through data pre-processing, SMOTE based class balance, hybrid ensemble learning and XAI methods. Trained form base solution, Ensemble with XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost for prediction performance; SHAP based global interpretability; LIME – provide local explanations. Additionally, it contains a human resource heads-up display module that converts predictive projections into multiple tiers of concrete workforce guidance. Experimental results show that the proposed model can take advantage of its superior indexing performance over traditional machine learning based models while gaining higher explanatory power and managerial relevance. With the proposed framework, it attempts to connect predictive intelligence and real-time workforce decision-making which will contribute in expedite progress of explainable as well data-driven human resource analytics.
Notes: The study concerns employee attrition in a workforce, using an HR analytics dataset; OSS projects or ecosystems are not the population.

Author: A. M; D. K; A. H. T; M. M
Title: Climashield: An Integrated Framework for Climate Data Anomaly Detection and Image Tampering Verification
Abstract Note: For accurate environmental monitoring, climate data must be reliable. However, current research often looks at finding anomalies in numerical data and finding tampering in satellite images as two different problems. This separation is a big problem because it leaves holes in the integrity of end-to-end data. To fix this, we suggest ClimaShield, a two-module system that combines SHA-256 and metadata-driven image tampering verification with Isolation Forest-based anomaly detection. The system has a modular architecture based on Streamlit. It has a data input layer, processing layer, visualization layer, and reporting layer that all work together to make it easy to use. Case studies using open-source datasets demonstrate ClimaShield's ability to accurately identify anomalous climate readings and detect subtle manipulations in satellite imagery. Despite its effectiveness, current constraints include limited coverage of advanced image forgeries and a lack of real-time processing. Planned improvements include incorporating deep learning models, GAN-based forgery detection, and blockchain-backed data provenance. In conclusion, ClimaShield represents a holistic, scalable, and secure solution that enhances confidence in climate data by addressing both numerical and visual integrity within a unified platform. However, these methods are practical only for string-based manipulation and not able to flesh out deep image forgeries in real-time. We outline proposed enhancements such as deep learning models, GAN based forgery detection and blockchain based data provenance. In summary, ClimaShield is a comprehensive solution that scales well and is secure to help you trust your climate data.
Notes: The study develops a climate-data integrity platform using open-source datasets; it does not investigate OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: N. K. M; C. B.H
Title: Detecting Nmap Scans Using Wireshark: A Comparative Study
Abstract Note: This paper presents a comprehensive comparative study on the detection of various Nmap scan techniques using Wireshark, an open-source network protocol analyzer widely adopted in cybersecurity analysis. Network scanning, particularly using tools like Nmap, forms the reconnaissance backbone of many cyberattacks. Understanding and identifying the behavior of such scans at the packet level is essential for strengthening network defense mechanisms. In this study, both active and stealth scan types—specifically SYN, TCP Connect, NULL, FIN, and Xmas scans—were executed in a controlled virtual environment using Kali Linux as the attacker and Ubuntu Linux as the target. Wireshark was used to capture and analyze the resulting traffic, with a focus on TCP header flag behaviors and the application of custom display filters for accurate detection. The analysis shows that active scans are highly detectable due to their standard handshake behavior, while stealth scans manipulate TCP flags to avoid detection, yet still leave identifiable anomalies in the packet structure. Results are presented through comparative visibility metrics, and the effectiveness of Wireshark's filtering capabilities is highlighted. The study concludes that, despite their evasive nature, stealth scans can be detected with precise packet-level inspection. Additionally, the paper discusses implications for network intrusion detection systems and proposes future research involving integration with machine learning models and real- time monitoring tools. This work provides practical insights for cybersecurity professionals aiming to enhance early-stage reconnaissance detection through open-source packet analysis tools.
Notes: The study evaluates network-scan detection using Wireshark; open-source software is a tool, not the subject of an OSS lifecycle or abandonment-related investigation.

Author: A. Arsenopoulos; V. Marinakis; K. Koasidis; A. Stavrakaki; J. Psarras
Title: Decision Support Tools for Energy Efficiency Obligated Parties towards Energy Poverty Alleviation
Abstract Note: Energy poverty is broadly understood as the inability of households to maintain adequate levels of energy services at an affordable cost, within an economically developed national context. Under the Energy Efficiency Directive (2012/27/EU), Member States must set up an energy efficiency obligation scheme that requires energy companies to achieve yearly energy savings in terms of annual sales to final consumers (Article 7). As such, energy companies need to design and implement measures that help final consumers improve the energy efficiency of their dwellings. A share of measures is required to be implemented as a priority among vulnerable households, including those affected by energy poverty, and where appropriate, in social housing. In this context, the aim of this paper is to present decision support tools to help utilities and energy suppliers effectively: (a) identify energy poor households; (b) select the most appropriate schemes to include under their Energy Efficiency Obligation and elaborate Energy Poverty Action Plans; (c) monitor their effectiveness and evaluate their impact. In this way, the proposed tools support utilities and energy suppliers to fulfil their energy efficiency obligations, as well as improve public relations, promote Corporate Social Responsibility strategies, reduce debt and overhead in managing debt and enhance their public image.
Notes: The study concerns energy companies, utilities, and energy-poor households, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: Z. Yang; C. Wang; P. Li; H. Wang; C. Liu
Title: Generative-enhanced distributionally robust power system optimization with carbon awareness
Abstract Note: As renewable energy fundamentally renovates the underlying logic and systemic architecture of the power systems, the intermittency and variability of low-carbon energy sources are becoming increasingly prominent. It has become an urgent priority to integrate both uncertain characteristics of power outputs and carbon emissions into optimal power flow (OPF) analysis. This study proposes an extended Wasserstein metric-based distributionally robust optimization (W-DRO) model by integrating hidden Markov model-based Time Series Generative Adversarial Networks (HMM-TSGAN). The proposed methodology reformulates the ambiguity set of uncertain parameters by synthesizing and over-sampling the empirical dataset, which effectively characterizes the uncertainties of renewable energy outputs and system emissions through the Wasserstein ball with potential supported distributions covered. The low-carbon oriented multi-objective OPF problem is then established, balancing sustainability and cost efficiency. Several optimization solutions are developed and integrated within an open-source architecture implemented, which ensures the scalability and the replicability of the proposed model. The accuracy, robustness, and sensitivity have been sufficiently validated via multiple IEEE testing systems, compared with diverse existing DRO models. Furthermore, the practical insights of the proposed architecture have been verified via the real-world meteorological information, actual provincial power grid parameters, and annual planning schemes.
Notes: The study develops power-system optimization methods; its open-source architecture is an implementation feature, not an OSS project lifecycle or maintenance subject.

Author: K. Tharindu; M. Abeysinghe; S. Karunarathne; K. Dilshan; D. Primal; A. Jayakody
Title: Autonomous Water Quality Monitoring: Integrating UWB Ad-Hoc Networks, Sensor Calibration, and Kubernetes Cloud Architecture
Abstract Note: Water quality monitoring plays a critical role in ensuring environmental sustainability and public health.
