Traditional methods, while accurate, are time-consuming and lack the ability to provide real-time insights. This study proposes a secure, scalable IoT-based solution utilizing autonomous sensor-equipped boats designed to measure pH, turbidity, and temperature in aquatic environments. The boats navigate predefined grid coordinates generated through a Python-based script and communicate data using UWB in a decentralized ad hoc network operating under the AODV routing protocol. Preprocessed sensor data is transmitted to a base station and securely forwarded to a Kubernetes-based cloud infrastructure for real-time processing and visualization. Communication between the base station and cloud services is secured using HTTPS/TLS encryption. Experimental trials confirm reliable navigation, high sensor accuracy, low latency, and robust security. The system remains cloud-agnostic and is compatible with a range of open-source Kubernetes distributions, enabling deployment flexibility across various environments. This research demonstrates an effective, autonomous approach to real-time water quality monitoring, advancing scalable and sustainable environmental management.
Notes: The study concerns an IoT water-quality monitoring system; open-source Kubernetes is only a deployment option, with no OSS lifecycle or maintenance topic studied.

Author: M. S; K. S; M. V; KamalrajSubramaniam
Title: Cell Anaemia Detection using Vision Transformer
Abstract Note: Sickle Cell Anaemia (SCA) is a inherited hematological disorder identified by deformation of red blood cells into a crescent-like shape, which significantly impairs oxygen-carrying capacity and leads to vaso-occlusive crises, organ damage, and chronic complications. Accurate and early detection is important for timely intervention and disease management. However, these models often rely heavily on handcrafted features and comprehensive preprocessing, reducing their scalability and generalization. Introduced research utilizes computerized model called Vision Transformer (ViT-B16), which is designed for medical images and detects sickle cell anemia. The model was first trained on a vast set of general images and then retrained using two open-source Kaggle datasets that contain microscope pictures of healthy and sickle-shaped red blood cells. Unlike older methods that required experts to manually select image features, this system learns directly from the raw images on its own, making the process faster and more structured. The tests showed that the model was highly accurate, correctly identifying sickle cells about 97.5 percentage , with a near-perfect AUC score of 0.99, showing its strong capability to differentiate between normal and abnormal cells. Other measures, like precision, recall, F1score, and the confusion matrix, further confirmed that the model is reliable and holds for practical use in clinical diagnosis. The system offers rapid inference, minimal preprocessing, and strong generalization across diverse samples, making it more suitable for deployment in real-time diagnostic workflows.
Notes: The study concerns medical-image diagnosis of sickle cell anaemia; open-source Kaggle datasets are only data sources, not OSS projects or ecosystems under study.

Author: M. Omri; M. Jooshaki; A. Abbaspour; M. Fotuhi-Firuzabad
Title: Evaluating the Impact of Operation Scheduling Methods on Microgrid Reliability Using Monte Carlo Simulation
Abstract Note: This paper provides a general methodology for evaluating the reliability of microgrids embedding conventional and renewable energy sources (RESs), as well as energy storage systems (ESSs). The developed reliability assessment model is then leveraged to investigate the impact of different resource scheduling methods on the reliability. The technique applied in this article to assess microgrid reliability is based on the sequential Monte Carlo simulation. In this approach, the coincidence of faults is considered, aside from the annual generation pattern of RESs, i.e., wind and photovoltaic, and the network load profiles. For the sake of considering priority of the microgrid loads, two categories, namely critical and normal demand, are modeled. Open-source MATPOWER Optimal Scheduling Tool (MOST) is employed for optimal management of available energy resources during network contingencies. The developed reliability assessment framework is implemented on two test microgrids. The simulation results prove that the scheduling method of the ESSs can have a significant impact on the reliability of the microgrids and continuous supply of the critical loads.
Notes: The study population is energy microgrids; open-source software is used only as a tool, not studied as an OSS project or ecosystem.

Author: P. Khan; R. Umer; Fatima; J. Muhammad; Z. Rauf; H. Ghafoor
Title: Forecasting Groundwater Depletion in Quetta Sub-Basin using Remote Sensing Data: Deep Learning Approach
Abstract Note: Groundwater resource is the largest freshwater storage resource, and it is also the largest storage for most human usage via domestic, industrial, and agricultural water supply and has maintained global food and water security. Therefore, it’s important to sustain the supply and demand to balance the huge population. Pakistan is one of the largest groundwater consumers in the region of South Asia, which extracts roughly 60 billion m3, and Pakistan’s groundwater table is dropping a meter per year. Groundwater has been over-exploited for drinking and agriculture. Balochistan is the country’s largest province by size but the smallest by population; the situation is worse than in other regions of the country because groundwater level (GWL) is declining at a pace of 2 to 3 m per year. The primary goal of this research is to anticipate GWL changes and depletion, as well as to evaluate various machine learning techniques in predicting the best deep learning models for forecasting GWL changes utilizing GRACE and GLDAS data in the Quetta District of Balochistan. Deep learning models are used to predict aquifers’ water-balancing capacities. The proposed approach would use data modeling with groundwater levels and meteorological factors as training parameters. By combining advanced groundwater modeling techniques and various datasets, the study aims to provide insights and implications for the entire research area. The ultimate goal is to develop effective management measures and ensure a sustainable supply of groundwater to support the needs of the large population in Balochistan, Pakistan, and the region of South Asia as a whole.
Notes: The study concerns groundwater depletion and forecasting in Pakistan, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: A. Flamini; L. Ciurluini; R. Loggia; A. Massaccesi; C. Moscatiello; L. Martirano
Title: A Prototype of Low-Cost Home Automation System for Energy Savings and Living Comfort
Abstract Note: In order to put into practice the objectives proposed by the policy of energy transition towards systems and buildings increasingly electrified, smart and sustainable, the massive digitization of environments and systems in both residential and commercial plays a key role, in view of the ‘internet of things.’ This paper aims to demonstrate the possibility of creating a reliable and robust building automation and monitoring system, maintaining, at the same time, a character of cost-effectiveness essential for a massive spread of these technologies. A case study has been realized by taking as reference a typical home in which smart devices have been placed, aimed at equipment controlling and widespread energy consumption monitoring, both electrical and thermal. The main environmental parameters influencing energy processes are also monitored, such as: position of the windows (open/closed), temperature and humidity of the individual areas air, levels of illuminance and the presence of people in the rooms and in the entire building. These elements were then integrated into the open-source SCADA (or better personal hub) “Home Assistant” and made available on a very simple dashboard, locally accessible through any web browser. As we will see, the complete low-cost smartization of the house brings a considerable advantage on energy savings, as well as an obvious greater comfort for users.
Notes: Home Assistant is used as an open-source platform for a building-automation case study; the study does not examine the OSS project's lifecycle or maintenance.

Author: M. G. Pleszkoch; R. C. Linger
Title: Improving network system security with function extraction technology for automated calculation of program behavior
Abstract Note: Malicious attacks on systems are a threat to business, government, and defense. Many attacks exploit system behavior unknown to the developers who created it. In today's state of art, software engineers have no practical means to determine how a sizable program will behave in all circumstances of use. This sobering reality lies at the heart of many problems in security and survivability. If full behavior is unknown, so too are embedded errors, vulnerabilities, and malicious code. This paper describes function-theoretic foundations for automated calculation of full program behavior. These foundations treat program control structures as mathematical functions or relations. The function, or behavior, of control structures can be abstracted in a stepwise process into procedure-free expressions that specify their net functional effects. Problems of computability and complexities of language semantics appear to have engineering solutions. Automated behavior calculation will add rigor to security and survivability engineering.
Notes: The study concerns automated program-behavior calculation for security engineering, not OSS project abandonment or a lifecycle-related concept.

Author: Paula Bialski
Title: Middle Tech: Software Work and the Culture of Good Enough
Abstract Note: Why software isn’t perfect, as seen through the stories of software developers at a run-of-the-mill tech companyContrary to much of the popular discourse, not all technology is seamless and awesome; some of it is simply “good enough.” In Middle Tech, Paula Bialski offers an ethnographic study of software developers at a non-flashy, non-start-up corporate tech company. Their stories reveal why software isn’t perfect and how developers communicate, care, and compromise to make software work—or at least work until the next update. Exploring the culture of good enoughness at a technology firm she calls “MiddleTech,” Bialski shows how doing good-enough work is a collectively negotiated resistance to the organizational ideology found in corporate software settings.The truth, Bialski reminds us, is that technology breaks due to human-related issues: staff cutbacks cause media platforms to crash, in-car GPS systems cause catastrophic incidents, and chatbots can be weird. Developers must often labor to patch and repair legacy systems rather than dream up killer apps. Bialski presents a less sensationalist, more empirical portrait of technology work than the frequently told Silicon Valley narratives of disruption and innovation. She finds that software engineers at MiddleTech regard technology as an ephemeral object that only needs to be good enough to function until its next iteration. As a result, they don’t feel much pressure to make it perfect. Through the deeply personal stories of people and their practices at MiddleTech, Bialski traces the ways that workers create and sustain a complex culture of good enoughness.
Notes: The study explicitly examines developers at a corporate technology company, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: N. Josselyn; B. Yin; T. Considine; J. Kelley; B. Rinderspacher; R. Jensen; J. Snyder; Z. Zhang; E. Rundensteiner
Title: Transferring Indoor Corrosion Image Assessment Models to Outdoor Images via Domain Adaptation
Abstract Note: Corrosion of materials impacts critical economic sectors from infrastructure, transportation, defense, health, to the environment. The development of safe anti-corrosive materials is thus an important area of study in materials science. Corrosion science of preparing materials and then monitoring their corrosion under adverse conditions is labor intensive, time consuming, and extremely costly. While deep learning has become popular in automating various engineering tasks, the development of deep models for corrosion assessment is lacking. We are the first to study deep domain adaptation (DA) models for the automated assessment of the corrosion status of anti-corrosive materials. Corrosion data, i.e., photographic images of treated corroding materials, is abundant when produced in artificially controlled laboratory settings, while corrosion image data sets from rich natural outdoor environments are more challenging to produce and thus much smaller. We leverage the more readily available indoor corrosion data to train a classifier and then transfer it via deep domain adaptation to also perform well on the small yet more realistic outdoor corrosion image data set – without requiring target labels. We empirically compare 5 popular domain adaptation models on real-world corrosion image data sets. Our study finds that DA achieves 27% improvement in test accuracy compared to the performance of the no-DA baseline for classifying real-world outdoor corrosion data.
Notes: The study population is corrosion images of anti-corrosive materials, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: T. U. Hassan; A. B. Khurram; S. Iqbal; A. W. Malik; M. M. Fraz
Title: Resolving Community Parking Issues: An IoT Enabled Statistical and Deep Learning Approach for Enhanced Urban Parking Management
Abstract Note: Parking challenges significantly impact urban communities, costing drivers time, fuel, and frustration while contributing to carbon dioxide emissions and congestion. Efficient parking management offers profit opportunities. With the rise of software-defined vehicles in smart cities, the Internet of Things (IoT) and Internet of Vehicles (IoV) are crucial for city navigation. Existing device-based solutions fail to assess financial impacts and scalability. We propose 11We open-source our work at: https://github.com/tayyibgondal/Parking_ Management_using_Predictive_Learning. git an IoT-enabled smart parking management framework using a real-time negotiation system. It integrates software-defined vehicles and Parking Side Units (PSUs) to enhance decision-making. Unlike previous studies, our model focuses both on maximizing revenue generated by parking lots, while also minimizing congestion of traffic on the roads. Moreover, we implemented a dynamic pricing policy scheme which imposes more fees to drivers during peak hours for parking. The peak hours for a particular day are determined in advance by forecasting the revenue for a particular day in advance by Seasonal Auto-regressive moving average(SARMIA) model. SARIMA model is compared with other machine learning techniques for our revenue forecasting and peak hour detection problem, and we chose it in our model as it performed the best. Our algorithm results in much better performance across different metrics such as number of vehicles roaming in search of a parking space at a time, request acceptance duration, remaining parking slots etc.
Notes: The study evaluates an open-source smart-parking framework for revenue, congestion, and parking performance, not OSS project lifecycle or maintenance.

Author: A. Flamini; L. Ciurluini; R. Loggia; A. Massaccesi; C. Moscatiello; L. Martirano
Title: Designing a Home Automation System Low-Cost for Energy Savings And Living Comfort
Abstract Note: In order to put into practice the objectives proposed by the policy of energy transition towards systems and buildings increasingly electrified, smart and sustainable, the massive digitization of environments and systems in both residential and commercial plays a key role, in view of the ‘internet of things’. This paper aims to demonstrate the possibility of creating a reliable and robust building automation and monitoring system, maintaining, at the same time, a character of cost-effectiveness essential for a massive spread of these technologies. A case study has been realized by taking as reference a typical home in which smart devices have been placed, aimed at equipment controlling and widespread energy consumption monitoring, both electrical and thermal. Also the main environmental parameters influencing energy processes are monitored, such as: position of the windows (open/closed), temperature and humidity of the individual areas air, levels of illuminance and the presence of people in the rooms and in the entire building. These elements were then integrated into the open source SCADA (or better personal hub) “Home Assistant” and made available on a very simple dashboard, locally accessible through any web browser. As we will see, the complete low-cost smartization of the house brings a considerable advantage on energy savings, as well as an obvious greater comfort for users.
Notes: The study uses Home Assistant as an open-source platform for a home-automation case study; it does not investigate the OSS project’s lifecycle, maintenance, or sustainability.

Author: V. Capparella; E. Nerio Nemmi; S. Violino; C. Costa; S. Figorilli; L. Moscovini; F. Pallottino; C. Pane; A. Mei; L. Ortenzi
Title: VIE-Net: Regressive U-Net for Vegetation Index Estimation
Abstract Note: Vegetation indexes (VIs) are important indicators in agriculture, revealing valuable information about the vegetative status of crops through nondestructive evaluation methods. Among these indexes, the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is a key metric used for assessing plant cover and health by combining Near-Infrared (NIR) and Red reflectance. NDVI calculation is based on multispectral cameras equipped with NIR sensors. However, the presence of this sensor is what makes the device costly and therefore impractical for small-scale farms. To address this limitation, recent works have explored the use of artificial intelligence to build AI-powered RGB cameras as a more affordable alternative for NDVI estimation. This has been done by means of generative artificial intelligence (often prone to hallucinations) or via shallow neural networks (pixel-wise regression) with the drawback of a high computational cost. Here, we introduce an end-to-end non-generative approach for NDVI estimation from calibrated RGB images. The proposed model, called VIE-Net, is a convolutional neural network based on a regressive version of the U-Net architecture. The model is tested on two datasets with images captured at 25 m above ground level (remote sensing) and 1 meter from the subject (proximal sensing), achieving correlation performance up to  $r^{2} = 0.98$  when non-vegetative background is removed. A lightweight version of the model was also tested, achieving  $r^{2} = 0.84$ . This approach not only provides a cost-effective solution for NDVI estimation but also improves the reliability of vegetation health assessment using standard RGB images.
Notes: The study concerns agricultural vegetation-index estimation using RGB images and neural networks, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: J. Jin; A. Song; H. Gong; Y. Xue; M. Du; F. Dong; J. Luo
Title: Distributed storage system for electric power data based on Hbase
Abstract Note: Managing massive electric power data is a typical big data application because electric power systems generate millions or billions of status, debugging, and error records every single day. To guarantee the safety and sustainability of electric power systems, massive electric power data need to be processed and analyzed quickly to make real-time decisions. Traditional solutions typically use relational databases to manage electric power data. However, relational databases cannot efficiently process and analyze massive electric power data when the data size increases significantly. In this paper, we show how electric power data can be managed by using HBase, a distributed database maintained by Apache. Our system consists of clients, HBase database, status monitors, data migration modules, and data fragmentation modules. We evaluate the performance of our system through a series of experiments. We also show how HBase's parameters can be tuned to improve the efficiency of our system.
Notes: The study evaluates an HBase-based system for processing electric power data; it does not investigate OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: T. M. Deserno; N. Stachowiak; J. Wang
Title: Beyond a Three-Dimensional Digital Rescue Sheet
Abstract Note: Traffic accidents occur all over the world. They are still among the most frequent causes of death. Introducing electrical vehicles or hydrogen fuel cells, the diversity of cars increases while more and more dangerous components are integrated into the vehicle. If such a vehicle needs brute force opening, these components impede occupants and rescue team. The rescue sheet is a paper-based document indicating location and site of dangerous components for extrication. It needs to be retrieved from databases once the vehicle type is identified. In this paper, we develop a three-dimensional (3D) digital rescue sheet that is based on a standardized terminology of dangerous items and a small set of 3D vehicle models. Our database feeds a mobile app for interactive visualization on smartphones and tablet computers. This core system can be extended by (i) guided optimal navigation (ii) automatic car type identification, and, based on CAN bus information, (iii) vehicle's deformation estimation, (iv) personalized injury estimation, and (v) a comprehensive accident registry. Furthermore, (vi) using the International Standard Accident Number (ISAN), all information can be sent to the rescue team before approaching the accident site. Our system is developed open source and can be extended with further components. It will speed up the rescue process and help to deliver the patients to the hospital within the golden hour.
Notes: The study develops an open-source vehicle-rescue application; it does not investigate OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: J. Hu; M. Zhang; B. Liu; Y. Wu; Y. Chen
Title: A Language-guided Acceleration Method for Smoke Testing of Game Quests
Abstract Note: Game quest is a common play in a massively multiplayer online role-playing game (MMORPG), which requires a player to take a series of actions and achieve multiple goals to accomplish it. During the game development life cycle, game companies often create and maintain a large number of releases, updates and tweaks of the game. There is a critical need for efficient smoke testing techniques to swiftly verify the core functionalities of the game. However, due to the vast number of game quests, existing smoke testing techniques typically incur a lot of time and labor costs. In this paper, we present an automated testing framework, named LAnguage-Guided somkE Testing (LAGET), which combines online planning with natural language models to efficiently find optimal policies for accomplishing the quest so that the testing process can be significantly accelerated. First, the online planning is, essentially, a model-based approach, and it dynamically constructs a game environment model, and computes the optimal solution for the smoke testing. Second, LAGET leverages the text description of the quest and adopts natural language models to guide better exploration in the game. Experimental results in both an open-source mini-game and two real industrial MMORPGs demonstrate that our method outperforms baseline methods by around 30% to 60%.
Notes: The study evaluates automated smoke testing for game quests; the open-source mini-game is only one test setting, with no OSS lifecycle or maintenance-continuity focus.

Author: L. Schaelicke; J. C. Freeland
Title: Characterizing sources and remedies for packet loss in network intrusion detection systems
Abstract Note: Network intrusion detection is becoming an increasingly important tool to protect critical information and infrastructure from unauthorized access. Network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) are commonly based on general-purpose workstations connected to a network tap. However, these general-purpose systems, although cost-efficient, are not able to sustain the packet rates of modern high-speed networks. The resulting packet loss degrades the system's overall effectiveness, since attackers can intentionally overload the NIDS to evade detection. This paper studies the performance requirements of a commonly used open-source NIDS on a modern workstation architecture. Using full-system simulation, this paper characterizes the impact of a number of system-level optimizations and architectural trends on packet loss, and highlights the key bottlenecks for this type of network-intensive workloads. Results suggest that interrupt aggregation combined with rule set pruning is most effective in minimizing packet loss. Surprisingly, the workload also exhibits sufficient locality to benefit from larger level-2 caches as well. On the other hand, many other common architecture and system optimizations have only a negligible impact on throughput.
Notes: The study evaluates performance and packet loss in an open-source NIDS, not the NIDS project's maintenance, continuity, or abandonment.

Author: E. Neofytou; S. P. Neophytides; M. Eliades; C. Papoutsa; M. Tzouvaras; D. G. Hadjimitsis
Title: A Review Of Soil Organic Carbon (SOC) Prediction Techniques In Agricultural Lands Using Remote Sensing
Abstract Note: The geological, ecological, and biological ecosystems of the planet have changed because of the global climate crisis, and this poses a serious threat to humanity as well as the conservation of agricultural productivity and food security. The European Commission outlined the continent's objective to become climate neutral by 2050 with zero net Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions. Soil organic carbon (SOC) is closely related to soil quality and has a significant impact on how soil and plants interact. SOC monitoring gives a unique role in agricultural sustainability thus precise prediction and monitoring of SOC is essential. Remote Sensing (RS) evolution, big data accessibility and Deep Learning (DL) architectures present enormous potential for extensive SOC monitoring. Several RS applications (e.g., Sentinels, MODIS, Landsat etc.) along with machine learning and DL methodologies (e.g., RF, ANN, CNN etc.) used in literature for SOC prediction. The current review paper emphasizes on the latest RS approaches used for SOC monitoring.
Notes: The review concerns remote sensing methods for soil organic carbon in agricultural lands, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: R. Beniwal; Parshant; N. Kumar; N. Rathore
Title: Digital Fencing – A Solution to Animal-Human Conflict
Abstract Note: Fencing of animals is vital because of several factors such as providing safety and protection to them, containing them, preventing the spread of illness, and avoiding animal-human conflict. However, physical fencing of animals has various challenges such as being time-consuming, expensive, unmaintainable, and in some cases ineffective also. Therefore, in this research paper, we propose a digital fencing mechanism using a Deep Learning algorithm to tackle the abovementioned challenges. To be particular, we design a ready-to-use version of yoloV5, which aims at providing a reliable, secure, and easy-to-implement solution for the animal-human conflict. Moreover, we used an object detection technique for the classification of the animals that come in a certain region covered by the cameras. Thus, our approach does not affect animal rights as they are not being continuously tracked like the GPS and other methods of prevention unless they appear in a restricted area. Hence, this concept of digital fencing can do miraculous work in this field as it can help farmers protect their farms without investing too much effort and time and by also keeping the required safety measures for the animals as well as for themselves. To implement this work, we created our own dataset of 10,000 images belonging to seven different categories of animals. As a result, we achieved classification with a precision of 0.872, recall of 0.858, mAP@0.5 of 0.904, and mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.584.
Notes: The study concerns an animal-fencing application and its custom image dataset, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: Y. El Asri; A. Lassioui; H. El Fadil; A. Hasni; M. El Ancary; H. Abbade; M. Chiheb
Title: Cost-Effective DIY Hardware Solutions for Experimental Validation of Renewable Energy and Electrical Energy Systems
Abstract Note: Experimental validation is essential in renewable energy emulators and energy storage systems to ensure reliability and practical implementation. However, high costs of AC/DC converters, measurement circuits, and microcontroller-based control platforms limit accessibility, especially in developing regions. This paper proposes cost-effective hardware and software solutions for validating renewable energy systems and storage management, using affordable power converters, data acquisition tools, and open-source control platforms. These strategies provide a scalable alternative to expensive setups, enabling researchers to perform accurate validations with minimal investment, thereby enhancing research credibility and advancing sustainable energy technologies.
Notes: The study concerns affordable experimental validation of renewable-energy systems; open-source control platforms are only tools, with no OSS lifecycle or maintenance topic.

Author: S. Shehbaz; M. Mehabadi; K. B. Kent
Title: Evaluating Time Series Databases Across Wide and Narrow Schema Designs for Appliance-Level Residential Energy Monitoring
Abstract Note: Appliance-level residential energy monitoring generates high-frequency, high-dimensional time series data that places significant demands on ingestion throughput, storage efficiency, and query performance. While time series databases (TSDBs) are widely used for such workloads, the impact of schema design—wide versus narrow—remains under-explored in the context of residential energy analytics. This paper presents a systematic benchmark of five open-source TSDBs—TimescaleDB, ClickHouse, QuestDB, InfluxDB v1.8, and Apache IoTDB—evaluating their suitability for appliance-level, per-minute energy data across five increasingly intensive workloads. Extending the TSM-Bench methodology, we assess ingestion latency, storage efficiency, and query performance for representative analytical patterns using point and analytical queries. Our results demonstrate that for these specific high-dimensional workloads, schema design can have a performance impact comparable to the underlying database architecture. Under our experimental configurations, wide schemas consistently outperformed narrow schemas across ingestion and query operations, while ClickHouse uniquely sustained efficient performance at the billion-row scale under both formats. These findings provide evidence-based guidance for TSDB selection and schema design, highlighting that the optimal database choice is highly dependent on the intersection of data dimensionality and intended schema format.
Notes: The study benchmarks open-source databases for energy-data performance and schema design, not OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: M. Almusawi; N. Bhatt; K. Kaur; A. K. Rai; V. Ravi Kishore; V. Kandpal
Title: AI for Cancer Detection
Abstract Note: Deep learning has proven beneficial in a number of healthcare sectors, including digital pathology, diagnostic imaging, pharmaceutical creation, hospitalization predictions, cancer and stromal cell classification, medical assistance, and more. A patient’s chances of survival are influenced by their cancer prognosis. due to the possibility of the sickness spreading. The clinical treatment that cancer patients get would be greatly improved with an accurate cancer prediction. The use of advanced mathematical modeling and machine learning techniques, which advance translational biology research, is primarily responsible for the creation of cancer prognostic projections. Processing power has increased significantly in recent years, and artificial intelligence technologies—deep learning in particular—have advanced quickly. Moreover, because large-scale next-generation sequencing is affordable and the data are accessible via open-source databases, there is an opportunity to develop more powerful and accurate models for cancer prognostic prediction.It is doable. In this study, we validated the most current research in this field and created a deep learning model to predict the prognosis of cancer. Deep learning has been proposed as a more comprehensive model that uses large amounts of data to provide more accurate predictions with less effort required for data processing. Studies have shown that the use of deep learning to cancer prognosis might equal or exceed the efficacy of existing methods such as Cox-PH. Deep learning is expected to improve cancer prediction by using multi-omics data, such as genomes, transcriptomics, and clinical cancer data.
Notes: The study concerns deep-learning methods for cancer prognosis; open-source databases are only a data source, with no OSS lifecycle or abandonment topic.

Author: T. Ablett; B. Chan; J. H. Wang; J. Kelly
Title: Efficient Imitation Without Demonstrations via Value-Penalized Auxiliary Control from Examples
Abstract Note: Common approaches to providing feedback in reinforcement learning are the use of hand-crafted rewards or full-trajectory expert demonstrations. Alternatively, one can use examples of completed tasks, but such an approach can be extremely sample inefficient. We introduce value-penalized auxiliary control from examples (VPACE), an algorithm that significantly improves exploration in example-based control by adding examples of simple auxiliary tasks and an above-success-level value penalty. Across both simulated and real robotic environments, we show that our approach substantially improves learning efficiency for challenging tasks, while maintaining bounded value estimates. Preliminary results also suggest that VPACE may learn more efficiently than the more common approaches of using full trajectories or true sparse rewards. Project site: https://papers.starslab.ca/vpace/.
Notes: The study concerns a reinforcement-learning algorithm evaluated in simulated and real robotic environments, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: J. Anderle; P. Schmitt; V. Tenta; R. Beneder
Title: From Code to Flight: Project-Oriented Learning with the COMET Multicopter and FLARE Framework
Abstract Note: Beginners in embedded and cyber-physical systems frequently face onboarding challenges, including heterogeneous microcontrollers, fragmented toolchains, and brittle build pipelines. Addressing these issues consumes valuable time and attention, fragments coursework, and erodes learner confidence. This paper describes a unified, classroom-ready hardware and software stack that combines a cost-efficient open multicopter platform (COMET) with an intentionally lightweight, FreeRTOS-based flight controller (FLARE). The application remains constant, while the computing platform varies, so the same flight-control software runs across multiple microcontroller families. This reduces re-onboarding by retaining a common Eclipse-based IDE workflow and preserving a coherent learning experience. Different microcontroller platforms allow alignment with course depth and student skill levels without changing the overarching experience. A deployment in university courses examines setup effort, student engagement, and feasibility under typical resource constraints. Preliminary observations indicate reduced integration overhead and sustained motivation when working with real hardware. This suggests that maintaining a stable application context while offering flexible hardware pathways can make embedded systems instruction more accessible, scalable, and resilient to toolchain complexity.
Notes: The study evaluates an embedded-systems teaching platform and learner experience; OSS is part of the implementation, with no project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment topic.

Author: A. Bashar; G. P. Parr; S. I. McClean; B. W. Scotney; M. Subramanian; S. K. Chaudhari; T. A. Gonsalves
Title: Employing Bayesian Belief Networks for energy efficient Network Management
Abstract Note: Network Management Systems (NMS) are used to monitor the network and along with Operations Support Systems (OSS) maintain the performance with a focus on guaranteeing sustained QoS to the applications and services. One aspect that is given less importance is the energy consumption of the network elements during the off peak periods. This paper looks at a scenario where the NMS plays an important role in making the network energy efficient by intelligently turning the network elements or their selective ports to sleep mode when they are underutilized. To this end, we propose and evaluate a Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) based Decision Management System (DMS), which provides intelligent decisions to the NMS for it to adaptively alter the operational modes of the network elements, without compromising the performance and QoS constraints. Simulated network has been used to provide the proof of concept followed by discussions on the amount of energy saved and its effect on the network performance.
Notes: The study concerns network management systems and energy efficiency in network elements; “OSS” refers to Operations Support Systems, not open-source software.

Author: A. A. Ardebili; A. Livera; G. E. Georghiou; A. Longo; A. Ficarella
Title: Data Generation for Photovoltaic Systems: Enhancing Accuracy with the Huld Model
Abstract Note: Gaps in current numerical models highlight challenges in accurately simulating photovoltaic (PV) systems, particularly their sensitivity to weather forecast outputs and the impact of environmental factors such as wind speed and humidity. These factors introduce discrepancies between simulated and real-life PV system performance. This study investigates the potential of open-source PV physical models, leveraging pvlib-python, to address these challenges. The research focuses on enhancing the accuracy of these models to generate synthetic data that closely replicate real-world conditions. Using the single diode equation implemented in pvlib-python, DC power production data from a real-life PV module is simulated, with initial discrepancies identified and mitigated through the integration of Huld model. This integration aims to improve the accuracy of synthetic data, thereby bridging the gap between simulated and actual performance metrics. The efficacy of the enhanced predictive models is evaluated using historical field measurements from a PV system testbed, demonstrating advancements in simulating PV system behaviors with enhanced accuracy and reliability. The results unveil a significant enhancement in synthetic data generation using PVLib and Huld model.
Notes: The study uses open-source PV models as tools to improve photovoltaic simulation accuracy; it does not investigate OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: A. Suryani; E. Agus Prasetio; N. Moonen; J. Popovic
Title: Stakeholder Perspectives on Microgrid Interoperability in Energy Access
Abstract Note: Interoperability is critical for the sustainability and scalability of decentralized energy systems. It facilitates self-coordination, component replacement, system expansion, upgrades, and integration with other systems, including the main grid. Despite its importance, achieving interoperability in the energy access sector remains a challenge, as stakeholders have diverse perspectives on approaches and strategies to achieve interoperability, creating further complexity. This study explores stakeholder perspectives on how microgrid interoperability can be achieved in the context of energy access, using Indonesia as a case study. To capture the diversity and subjectivity of expert opinions, the study employs the Q methodology, marking the first application of this method to the topic of interoperability. The study advances the theoretical understanding of interoperability in decentralized energy systems by revealing four distinct stakeholder perspectives, namely (1) Harmonization Promoters, (2) Industry Allies, (3) Tech Proponents, and (4) Public Advocates. Although there are some areas of consensus, stakeholders differ in their views on standardization, technical features, and stakeholder roles. These differences highlight the competing priorities that influence decision making on approaches to interoperability that balance technical, regulatory, and market considerations. This study provides practical insights for developing more inclusive and effective interoperability strategies, supported by empirical evidence derived from primary data gathered from relevant stakeholders.
Notes: The study examines microgrid interoperability and energy-access stakeholders, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: B. Sanghrajka; H. Maru; C. Doshi; A. Singh
Title: Architecting Operating System Frameworks for Self-Driving Vehicles
Abstract Note: The invention of self-driving automobiles represents the shift away from a purely mechanical-based vehicle system to one defined by software (cyber-physical platform). The vehicle's operating system (OS) and the virtualization layer both play a critical role in achieving the necessary reliability, safety, and intelligence that characterize a self-driving automobile. This study will conduct an investigation into the current state of the various OS architectures that are employed by the automotive industry (monolithic vs. microkernel), as well as an evaluation of the appropriateness of Type-1 hypervisors for use in mixed-criticality safety-critical systems; an analysis of current AUTOSAR Classic Platform and AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform development activity within the automotive OEM (original equipment manufacturer) community; the evolution of embedded OSs as they are integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) systems; and a review of currently known safety-certified Real-Time Operating Systems (RTOS) that are used in the development of automated vehicles. The primary contribution of this study lies in identifying an integrated cross-layer perspective that links operating system design to virtualization techniques (via hypervisors), and to System on Chip (SoC) functionality in autonomous vehicles. The research uses qualitative comparisons and industry case studies to demonstrate how these layers develop over time in support of software-defined vehicle architecture, thereby supporting Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 9 and 11 by providing a safer and more intelligent transportation system.
Notes: The study concerns automotive operating systems and platforms used in the automotive industry, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: Y. Li; J. Zeng; W. Wu; S. Zhou; Y. Zhang; Z. Zuo
Title: Collector Substations Location and Topology for Large Offshore Wind Farms Based on Wake Model
Abstract Note: Wind energy plays an increasingly pivotal role in the global energy landscape, serving as a key driver for energy transition and the pursuit of sustainable development. This paper innovatively introduces a dynamic K-means algorithm with particle swarm optimization(DKM-PSO) to autonomously determine the optimal number and locations of offshore substations (OSs) in large-scale offshore wind farms (LOWFs). Additionally, the paper use a binary particle swarm optimization(BPSO) technique to identify the most suitable cable routing topology. This approach considers the power flow direction and the spatial arrangement of the offshore wind farm, facilitating the effective transmission of electricity generated by the wind turbines(WTs) to the OS. The ultimate goal of this optimization is to enhance economic efficiency. The proposed design has been validated through testing on a large-scale offshore wind farm cluster model. The results indicate that the new method offers cost savings compared to previous approaches.
Notes: The study concerns offshore wind-farm infrastructure and optimization, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: S. D. L. Ferreira
Title: Durable Execution for AI Agents: A Design Pattern for Fault-Tolerant Agent Loops
Abstract Note: AI agents—autonomous systems that iteratively invoke tools and make decisions based on accumulated context—are increasingly deployed in mission-critical cloud applications. Yet when these agents fail due to infrastructure crashes, network issues, or service timeouts, they cannot reliably resume, leading to incomplete transactions, duplicated operations, or workflow abandonment.We present the Durable AI Agent Loop Architecture, a design pattern addressing this reliability gap through three primitives: deterministic control flow, managed side-effect abstraction, and event-sourced state persistence. Rather than relying on volatile checkpoints, this architecture records every operation as an immutable event before proceeding, ensuring state reconstruction after failures. By isolating non-deterministic operations (LLM calls and tool invocations) from orchestration logic, agents recover without redundant execution or logic drift.We validate this approach by testing resilience against reproducible failure scenarios—including worker process crashes, external service timeouts, and logic errors—on a reference implementation. Our analysis demonstrates that the architecture maintains state integrity across these failures, and performance measurements show that the durability overhead remains negligible relative to typical LLM inference times. We provide a reproducible open-source reference implementation to enable independent verification and practical adoption.
Notes: The study evaluates fault tolerance in AI-agent execution; its open-source reference implementation is a tool, not an OSS project lifecycle or maintenance subject.

Author: R. B. Lugina; F. D. Wijaya; Y. F. Sidik
Title: Comparison of Balanced and Unbalanced Conditions in Microgrid Test Bed
Abstract Note: This study discusses the impact of balanced and unbalanced operating conditions on a laboratory scale microgrid test bed developed for educational and research purposes. The system is designed to provide students with practical experience in microgrid operation while facilitating quantitative analysis of power quality parameters, including voltage, current, total harmonic distortion (THD), flicker, and symmetrical sequence components. Experimental scenarios were conducted with different load variations to simulate practical disturbances that cause imbalance. The results show that load imbalance can increase neutral current, harmonic distortion, zero-sequence components, and flicker levels, especially in the affected phase. By comparing the results with international standards, this study not only demonstrated unbalanced operating conditions but also provided an accessible platform for student learning and a practical framework for validating microgrid designs under laboratory conditions.
Notes: The study concerns a laboratory microgrid test bed and power-quality conditions, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: M. Martikka; S. Salo; K. Siilin; T. Ruohomäki; P. Tuomaala; E. Nykänen
Title: Smart City Resilience with Active Citizen Engagement in Helsinki
Abstract Note: New solutions sometimes face challenges in acceptance as improvements and active citizen engagement plays a key role of resilient smart city development. This paper describes a set of actions in Helsinki as part of mySMARTLife project that are aimed to engage citizens in interaction. The actions range from online services and mobile applications to hands-on equipment implementations. They are mainly described from the technological but also from an economic and a social point of view. All the activities are connected to the Helsinki action plan to render the city carbon neutral by 2035. Motivation through positive experience requires practical solutions and reachable goals for approval and impact in smart cities progress.
Notes: The study concerns citizen engagement and smart-city development in Helsinki, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: A. Gupta; M. Goyal
Title: A Comprehensive Review of Microsoft Semantic Kernel: Architecture, Capabilities, and Research Directions
Abstract Note: The incorporation of large language models (LLMs) in company software amplified the necessity for efficient AI orchestration systems. Microsoft Semantic Kernel is an optimized open-source system specifically for the implementation of LLMs in customary software systems. Despite its widespread popularity in corporate settings, specifically in Fortune 500 organizations, there is limited scientific research available pertaining to its architecture, characteristics, and disadvantages. This report gives an in-depth analysis of Semantic Kernel, including its fundamental constituents—kernel orchestration, plugin ecosystem, semantic memory, and agent framework—and implementations in multiple languages in C, Python, and Java. A comparative report with other frameworks like LangChain outlines the advantages of Semantic Kernel in maintaining dynamic and concurrent task orchestration. The work outlines key performance characteristics, integration possibilities, and current limitations and outlines useful insights into its applicability in practical AI engineering. In addition, the directions for future improvements are discussed in order to broaden the use in enterprise-scale AI systems.
Notes: The paper reviews an AI orchestration framework’s architecture and capabilities; it does not investigate OSS project abandonment, maintenance, continuity, or related lifecycle factors.

Author: M. A. Uzzaman
Title: Estimating ESS Revenue from Multiple Market Services in Finland's Electricity Market
Abstract Note: This study explores the potential revenue generation of energy storage systems (ESS) in the Nordic electricity markets, particularly in Finland. By utilising historical market data and the open-source QuEST valuation platform developed by Sandia National Laboratories, the study quantifies the profitability of ESS across day-ahead, intraday, and frequency regulation markets. Two scenarios are analyzed: arbitrage-only operations and a combined strategy incorporating arbitrage and frequency regulation services. The results highlight the significant role of ESS in capitalizing on price fluctuations and enhancing grid stability. Cross-border trading occurs as the dominant revenue source, followed by frequency regulation, while arbitrage offers a smaller yet critical contribution. The proposed methodology integrates optimization modeling with real-world market dynamics, offering a replicable and adaptable framework for assessing ESS profitability. This study provides practical insights for grid operators, investors, and policymakers aiming to enhance energy system flexibility and resilience in the Nordic context.
Notes: The study evaluates energy-storage profitability in electricity markets; open-source QuEST is only a valuation tool, with no OSS lifecycle or maintenance topic.

Author: S. Nirmal; K. Dhanvinesh; G. Saranya
Title: From Novice to Ninja: Novice to Ninja’s Guide to CTF Domains
Abstract Note: Capture The Flag (CTF) platforms provide an immersive and dynamic learning experience for those interested in becoming cybersecurity experts. There are no proper learning platforms that demonstrate how to approach these challenges at present. So, in this paper, the Novice to Ninja learning platform is crafted to provide guidance that simplifies comprehension for individuals, allowing even novices to understand and tackle challenges with ease. At the moment, Novice to Ninja guides the users with the following domains of CTF: Open Source Intelligence (OSINT), Cryptography, and Steganography. This platform is versatile in keeping up with the ever-evolving landscape of cyber dangers by providing an ever-growing library of problems and fostering a culture of ongoing learning and innovation.
Notes: The study presents a cybersecurity CTF learning platform; it does not examine OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: Z. Mahrez; E. Sabir; E. Badidi; W. Saad; M. Sadik
Title: Smart Urban Mobility: When Mobility Systems Meet Smart Data
Abstract Note: Cities around the world are expanding dramatically, with urban population growth reaching nearly 2.5 billion people in urban areas and road traffic growth exceeding 1.2 billion cars by 2050. The economic contribution of the transport sector represents 5% of the GDP in Europe and costs an average of US  $\$ $ 482.05 billion in the United States. These figures indicate the rapid rise of industrial cities and the urgent need to move from traditional cities to smart cities. This article provides a survey of different approaches and technologies such as intelligent transportation systems (ITS) that leverage communication technologies to help maintain road users safe while driving, as well as support autonomous mobility through the optimization of control systems. The role of ITS is strengthened when combined with accurate artificial intelligence models that are built to optimize urban planning, analyze crowd behavior and predict traffic conditions. AI-driven ITS is becoming possible thanks to the existence of a large volume of mobility data generated by billions of users through their use of new technologies and online social media. The optimization of urban planning enhances vehicle routing capabilities and solves traffic congestion problems, as discussed in this paper. From an ecological perspective, we discuss the measures and incentives provided to foster the use of mobility systems. We also underline the role of the political will in promoting open data in the transport sector, considered as an essential ingredient for developing technological solutions necessary for cities to become healthier and more sustainable.
Notes: The article surveys smart urban mobility, intelligent transportation, and urban data; OSS project lifecycle or abandonment is not studied.

Author: F. N. Tzortzoglou; A. A. Malikopoulos
Title: Teaching cars to drive
Abstract Note: In recent decades, society has witnessed significant advancements in emerging mobility systems. These systems refer to transportation solutions that incorporate digital technologies, such as, automation and connectivity, to support sustainability goals, creating safer, more efficient, and user-centered mobility. Examples include connected and automated vehicles (CAVs), shared mobility services (e.g., carpooling), electrified mobility solutions, and mobility-as-a-service platforms such as Whim, Moovit, and Uber. These innovations have the potential to greatly impact different aspects of mobility such as safety, pollution, comfort, travel time, and fairness. In this article, we explore the current landscape of CAVs. We discuss their role in daily life and their future potential, while also examining the challenges they may introduce. We further review practical challenges in CAVs research, with a focus on simulation and real-world testing of CAV algorithms. Then, existing solutions that aim to overcome these limitations are presented. Finally, we provide an accessible introduction to modeling CAVs using basic kinematic principles and offer an open source tutorial to motivate interested students to begin exploring the field.
Notes: The article surveys connected and automated vehicles and offers an open-source tutorial; it does not study OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: M. Zebboudj; D. Rekioua; T. Rekioua
Title: Comparative Optimal Dispatch Control Strategies for a Hybrid Renewable Energy System
Abstract Note: This research presents a study on a hybrid renewable energy system that integrates battery storage with photovoltaic panels, wind turbines, and a diesel generator. The study was conducted in Bejaia, Algeria, which possesses substantial potential for wind and solar energy resources. The integration of the diesel generator is essential as an auxiliary source to compensate for the intermittency of renewable resources, but it requires precise sizing according to daily peak load demands. The stand-alone system architecture is simulated under two different optimization algorithms using HOMER Pro (open-source version): combined dispatch (CD) and predictive dispatch (PS), to determine the optimal system cost. The impact of various component prices on the net present cost (NPC) and the cost of energy (COE), along with the emissions of polluting gases following diesel generator integration, were evaluated using sensitivity analysis. The results demonstrate that the predictive dispatch algorithm clearly outperforms the combined dispatch approach in optimizing investment costs, while the combined dispatch strategy achieves greater reductions in emissions and fuel consumption by the diesel generator.
Notes: The study concerns a renewable energy system; HOMER Pro is only a simulation tool, not the OSS population under study.

Author: J. Zeng; S. Jackson; I. -J. Lin; M. Gustafson; E. Hoarau; R. Mitchell
Title: Operations simulation of on-demand digital print
Abstract Note: On-demand digital print service is a form of personalized manufacturing service. Key to the commercial print value-creation chain is the responsive and accurate knowledge discovery and decision making throughout the service engagement and fulfillment between the content suppliers and the print service providers (PSP). The business model of on-demand print imposes a great challenge to the PSP factory design, production planning and management due to its intrinsic, highly volatile demand stream. It pushes the PSP resource planning and production management from a form of “tribal art” towards data driven management science. Operations simulation and its practice is an integral component of the data-driven decision making process, and is gaining growing significance. In this paper, we describe operations simulation of an end-to-end digital print process; we treat the management of print manufacturing as a heterogeneous, concurrent, integrated system, accounting for the performance, efficiency, stability, and sustainability as organic system attributes. We exhibit the comparison between the simulation results and the factory internal audit information and show good agreement.
Notes: The study concerns a commercial digital-print manufacturing process, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: M. Surya; D. Rajendran; S. G. Kumar; R. S. Dheeraj; M. Hariharasudhan; K. Gokul
Title: A Geo-Visual Exploration of Water Supply and Infrastructure in Semi-Urban Tamil Nadu
Abstract Note: This paper focuses on the geospatial discrepancies between water supply and demand systems in semi-urban Tamil Nadu, based on a geovisual analysis. The increase in the population, the fast development of cities, and the aging networks usually cause disproportions between the planned capacity and the provided service. In response to this, we incorporate municipal supply, census-based demand measures, and land-use measures that come out of satellite within a GIS framework. The analysis involves mapping of distribution networks, network overlay of supply-demand proxies and spatial statistics to determine clusters of service deficits. A dashboard created with an open-source can be explored by ward, season, and water source. Results indicate recurrent deficit in rapidly expanding wards outside of the legacy mains, increased non-revenue water close to lines near the end of life, seasonality of the tanker supply, and inequalities in the service hours based on the elevation and network endpoints. Scenario mapping shows that these disparities can be minimized through the application of specific remedies, including rainwater harvesting, reservoir augmentation, and pressure-zone rebalancing. The research provides a conceptualized, evidence-based, practical workflow to utilities, which planners can use to rank infrastructure upgrades. Nevertheless, the method helps make water management in semi-urban Tamil Nadu more progressive and fairer in the event of limited data.
Notes: The study examines water-supply infrastructure and service disparities; open-source software is only used to create a dashboard, with no OSS lifecycle or abandonment topic.

Author: A. Sousa; D. Beserra; J. Araujo
Title: Evaluating Software Aging Resistance in Serverless Computing Under Stress Workloads
Abstract Note: Serverless computing abstracts infrastructure management, enabling cost-efficient and scalable application deployment. However, multiple operations can be performed simultaneously, leading to system degradation of resources exhaustion during prolonged executions. This study assesses resource utilization in serverless environments using Knative, testing four OS-container engine configurations (Ubuntu/Docker, Ubuntu/Podman, Debian/Docker, Debian/Podman) under stress workload. Results show Ubuntu paired with Docker achieves optimal resource efficiency, avoids software aging, and maintains consistent performance, making it the most effective configuration for scalable serverless deployments. The absence of progressive degradation in resource metrics underscores serverless architectures’ potential to resist software aging through autoscaling. Findings provide actionable insights for optimizing resource management in open-source serverless platforms.
Notes: The study evaluates resource utilization and software-aging resistance in serverless configurations; it does not examine OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: R. Hema; S. Subbulakshmi; B. Veera Jyothi; R. Gurulakshmi; M. Vignesh; M. Blessy Queen Mary
Title: Smart Automated Irrigation through IoT Technology
Abstract Note: This work presents the development and implementation of an IoT-based automatic irrigation system designed to optimize water usage in agricultural settings. The system integrates a Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) with the Blynk platform to enable real-time monitoring and control of irrigation parameters, including soil moisture, water level, and ambient light. Using an Arduino UNO microcontroller and an ESP-8266 Wi-Fi module, the system collects and processes sensor data to automate irrigation based on predefined thresholds. The Blynk platform facilitates remote data visualization and system control through customizable dashboards, allowing for both automatic and manual adjustments. The proposed system demonstrates a cost-effective solution for improving irrigation efficiency and reducing water waste, with implications for sustainable agricultural practices.
Notes: The study concerns an IoT irrigation system in agriculture, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: P. J. Nair; R. Hadidi; S. Ganesh; S. Kodge; S. Rathore; N. Thanawala; N. Reddy; G. Saharia; V. Patankar; A. Tiruvur; N. Kurella; S. Bhoja
Title: Early Silicon of Raptor: The First 3D-DRAM Accelerator for Generative Inference
Abstract Note: Generative Inference is largely memory-bound. Autoregressive decoding dominates inference runtime and thus drives memory bandwidth and capacity demands. SRAM-based accelerators offer high bandwidth but limited capacity, while HBM DRAM provides capacity but is constrained by bandwidth and power. 3D-stacked logic-on-DRAM (3D-DRAM) helps close this gap, but integrating 3D-DRAM with accelerator logic introduces four challenges: (1) workload-aware mapping to exploit parallelism, (2) power optimization without burst-based data bus inversion (DBI), (3) resilience with high bank counts, and (4) thermal reliability at elevated junction temperatures. This paper distills lessons from the early silicon of Raptor, the first commercial generative inference accelerator with 3Dstacked DRAM (3D-DRAM). This paper introduces four key architectural features to enable practical 3D-DRAM integration. First, stream-blocking maps KV-cache streams onto configurable 3D-DRAM channels, sustaining up to 100 TB/s per card while preserving bank-level parallelism. Second, pinless DBI on the single-cycle $\mu$ bump interface reduces memory-subsystem energy. Third, topology-preserving redundancy with thermal-aware refresh. Fourth, interleaved ECC for reliability at high temperatures. Across Llama-3.1 70B, DeepSeek-V3, Kimi K2, GPT-OSS, Whisper, and Canary, Raptor 3D-DRAM gives $\mathbf{4. 7 1} \times$ and $\mathbf{2. 4 4} \times$ higher throughput than with HBM and SRAM, respectively, while being less sensitive to network latency and bandwidth.
Notes: The study concerns a commercial generative-inference hardware accelerator and its memory architecture, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: F. Castiglione; S. Vergara; G. Ramírez
Title: Python software to monitor NCRE generation systems
Abstract Note: Renewable energy use has been increased to reduce the environmental impact of fossil fuel-based generation. Monitoring these systems is important to detect anomalies and to determine its performance. Monitoring includes measurement, data management and visualization. This work describes a software platform to extract data from an existent energy analyser by Modbus TCP/IP protocol and saves them in a MySQL database. The platform provides a multiplatform access in a server-client structure. Client devices connected in the local network can visualize data graph by using a web navigator. The platform was built using Python open-source libraries.
Notes: The study describes a monitoring platform for renewable-energy systems; open-source libraries are only implementation tools, and OSS project lifecycle or maintenance is not studied.

Author: N. Kapre; B. Chandrashekaran; H. Ng; K. Teo
Title: Driving Timing Convergence of FPGA Designs through Machine Learning and Cloud Computing
Abstract Note: Machine learning and cloud computing techniques can help accelerate timing closure for FPGA designs without any modification to original RTL code. RTL is generally frozen closer to system delivery target to avoid injecting new unforeseen bugs or significantly affecting design characteristics. In these circumstances, developers trying to close timing are either at the mercy of random trials through placement seed exploration or through vendor-provided design space exploration tools that run a few compilation trials with changes to the CAD tool options (or parameters). Instead, we propose evaluating multiple CAD runs in parallel on the cloud, supported by a Bayesian learning and classification framework for generating multiple CAD parameter combinations most likFPGA CAD tool parametersely to help attain timing closure. We maintain a database of FPGA CAD tool parameters (input) along with associated variations in timing slack (output)to enable the learning process. A key engineering resource we use here is cheap and abundant parallelism made possible through cloud computing frameworks such as the Google Compute Engine. Across a range of open-source benchmarks, we show that learning helps improve total negative slack (TNS) scores by 10.5× (geomean) when compared to a single baseline run of Quart us 14.1 and by 7× (geomean) when compared to Alter a Quart us 14.1 Design Space Explorer (DSE).
Notes: The study evaluates FPGA design timing closure using open-source benchmarks; it concerns hardware design optimization, not OSS project lifecycle or software-engineering maintenance.

Author: G. Jati; A. A. S. Gunawan; S. W. Lestari; W. Jatmiko; M. H. Hilman
Title: Multi-sperm tracking using Hungarian Kalman Filter on low frame rate video
Abstract Note: One factor of human sperm health is sperm motility. Motility is the ability of sperm to move. Sperm with healthy motility move forward promptly, not inactive and not moving in circles. In this paper, we would like to analyse sperm motility by considering the problem of multi object tracking in video sequences of human sperms. The challenges in multi-sperm tracking are many human sperms have fast and unpredictable movement In addition, the sperm have similar size and shape comparing by each others. To solve this problem, we used sperm detection in each video sequence to get the position of sperms. In the same time, the estimated sperm position is calculated based on previous tracking by using Kalman Filter. Finally the positions of detected sperms are compared to estimation results by using Hungarian assignment method. In this way, the trajectory of each sperm can be conclude. This paper analyze sperm motility qualitatively based on the resulted sperm trajectories. The experiment results were conducted on both open video data and our own low-frame-rate video data. The experiment results shows that the proposed method can handle the challenges in multi sperm tracking, create their trajectory and then analyze their behaviors.
Notes: The study population is human sperm in video sequences, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: D. Martinez-Mosquera; L. Recalde; C. Tipantuna
Title: Building Cognitive Cities in Developing Countries: Ecuador Case Study
Abstract Note: Humans as sensors is the paradigm for transforming the idea of a “smart city” into the concept of a “cognitive city”. While the concept of smart cities is based on the notion of using technology to improve city life, cognitive cities take it a step further by utilizing the large amounts of data generated by people to make informed decisions. In developed countries, numerous projects have been successfully implemented using cognitive computing models in areas such as health, transport, and energy sustainability. However, in developing countries such as Ecuador, the collection of data is often a challenge, making it difficult to implement these types of projects. Therefore, in this paper, we present a comprehensive approach to identify available data sources, including open data, social media, and IoT networks, to start the path toward cognitive cities. Our main objective is to present and facilitate the understanding of those datasets by classifying them according to their context of use around their importance in a cognitive city. In this sense, this document consolidates 547 datasets from open portals and describes several proposals in which sensors generate data as part of the Internet of Things infrastructures. Besides, we corroborated that Twitter, Facebook, and Youtube are the most used online social networks in terms of e-participation mainly. We then identified the most relevant categories based on the data available from the analyzed data sources for cities in Ecuador. The results presented establish the need to understand, retrieve and use these data by government, academic, industrial, or research entities. Thus, decision-making processes may be implemented to improve the quality of life of citizens on the basis of available data and aim at building a cognitive country.
Notes: The study catalogs open datasets, social media, and IoT sources for cognitive-city decision-making; it does not examine OSS project lifecycle or abandonment-related concepts.

Author: N. Dhar; B. Deng; M. R. Islam; K. F. Ahmad Nasif; L. Zhao; K. Suo
Title: Activation Sparsity Opportunities for Compressing General Large Language Models
Abstract Note: Deploying local AI models, such as Large Language Models (LLMs), to edge devices can substantially enhance devices’ independent capabilities, alleviate the server’s burden, and lower the response time. Owing to these tremendous potentials, many big tech companies have been actively promoting edge LLM evolution and released several lightweight Small Language Models (SLMs) to bridge this gap. However, SLMs currently only work well on limited real-world applications. We still have huge motivations to deploy more powerful (larger-scale) AI models on edge devices and enhance their smartness level. Unlike the conventional approaches for AI model compression, we investigate from activation sparsity. The activation sparsity method is orthogonal and combinable with existing techniques to maximize compression rate while maintaining great accuracy. According to statistics of open-source LLMs, their Feed-Forward Network (FFN) components typically comprise a large proportion of parameters (around $\tfrac{2}{3}$). This internal feature ensures that our FFN optimizations would have a better chance of achieving effective compression. Moreover, our findings are beneficial to general LLMs and are not restricted to ReLU-based models.This work systematically investigates the tradeoff between enforcing activation sparsity and perplexity (accuracy) on state-of-the-art LLMs. Our empirical analysis demonstrates that we can obtain around 50% of main memory and computing reductions for critical FFN components with negligible accuracy degradation. This extra 50% sparsity does not naturally exist in the current LLMs, which require tuning LLMs’ activation outputs by injecting zero-enforcing thresholds. To obtain the benefits of activation sparsity, we provide a guideline for the system architect for LLM prediction and prefetching. Moreover, we further verified the predictability of activation patterns in recent LLMs. The success prediction allows the system to prefetch the necessary weights while omitting the inactive ones and their successors (compress models from the memory’s perspective), therefore lowering cache/memory pollution and reducing LLM execution time on resource-constraint edge devices.
Notes: The study optimizes activation sparsity and inference efficiency in LLMs; open-source models are only a data context, with no OSS lifecycle or maintenance topic.

Author: S. Eckhoff; H. Wagner; O. Werth; J. Gerlach; M. H. Breitner; B. Engel
Title: Electric mobility integration in energy communities: trending topics and future research directions
Abstract Note: The urgent need to reduce carbon emissions resulting in decentralized renewable energy systems also encourages the establishment of energy communities where residential and/or commercial consumers can actively participate in the generation, consumption, or provision of flexibility of electric energy. The integration of electric mobility within these energy communities is of particular interest as its increasing load will impact grid stability and therefore the power grid's and components' sizing and operation. With this work, we provide a holistic overview of research activities on the integration of electric vehicles in energy communities that supports researchers and practitioners with the identification of relevant topics and research gaps. We identify seven research clusters by hierarchical clustering analysis. Relevant topics include smart charging, vehicle-to-x, and considerations of uncertainty. Future research should focus on open-source models and the synthesis of the knowledge base from the extensive body of literature.
Notes: The study maps research on electric mobility in energy communities; open-source models are mentioned only as a future research direction, not as the subject of an OSS lifecycle study.

Author: M. Mashilo; T. Iyamu
Title: The openness of the concept of technology open innovation
Abstract Note: Generally, organisations continue to strive for sustainability and competitive advantage. This leads some of the organisations to employ various tactics and mechanisms in attempts to fulfill their aims and objectives, overtime. The challenges of sustainability and competitive advantage could also be attributed to organisations' reliance on technology which has increased significantly in recent years. The increasing competitiveness amongst the organisations drives technology innovations. As technology evolves, more organisations are challenged, hence the quest to explore the concept of open innovation. The paper focuses on the concept of open innovation from both academic and professional (corporate) perspectives. Through interpretivism philosophical assumption we sought an understanding of the impact and implications of the openness in the concept of open innovation.
Notes: The paper examines open innovation in organisations from academic and corporate perspectives, not OSS project lifecycle or abandonment-related concepts.

Author: K. M. R. Tabal
Title: Logistic Regression-Based Inattention Detection via EEG–IMU Sensor Fusion in Smart Headgear
Abstract Note: Cognitive monitoring plays an important role in improving safety and performance in transportation, construction, and other high-risk work environments. This study proposes a smart headgear system for real-time inattention detection, utilizing sensor fusion of single-channel EEG (ThinkGear™ ASIC Module) and inertial measurement unit (MPU6050). The system extracts and processes key physiological markers which include Theta/Beta ratio, Alpha/Beta ratio, and head movement dynamics (pitch and yaw) using a logistic regression model (L2-regularization, liblinear solver) optimized for embedded deployment. The L2 regularization helped to address complexity control and overfitting. The model was trained using the annotated EEG data (using open-source datasets from Kaggle) and simulated head movement data and was deployed on an ESP32 microcontroller for real-time, embedded inference. The system achieved 92.33% accuracy on a hold-out test set and 85.67% on unseen validation dataset composed of actual head movement data mimicking real-world scenarios with supporting metrics of 84.52% precision, 87.33% recall, 85.90% F1-score, and 0.86 ROC AUC. By combining low-cost hardware with efficient embedded processing, the proposed system offers the feasibility of a practical, fully wearable solution for cognitive monitoring in safety-critical work environments, with strong potential for application in long-distance driving.
Notes: The study develops an inattention-detection system for safety-critical work; open-source datasets are only a training resource, with no OSS lifecycle topic.

Author: S. Ajward; N. Jayasundara; S. Madushika; R. Ragel
Title: Converting printed Sinhala documents to formatted editable text
Abstract Note: Digitizing printed document is always a challenge faced by the computing society. Digitization of text not only allows users to easily modify and reprint printed documents, but also is a need of the day due to the use of word-search capability available at disposal in this era. Converting a printed document into a stream of characters using OCR (optical character recognition) techniques is a widely researched area of the past and there are a number of well established algorithms available in the literature to do so. However, the idea of preserving the formatting information of the original document is not much studied. The contribution of this paper is of two folds: (1) applying known OCR techniques to one of Sri Lanka's native languages, Sinhala, and addressing the challenges in doing so and (2) maintaining a number of selected formatting features of the printed document in the converted editable text. Therefore, this paper outlines the design and implementation of a software system that converts a scanned paper document written in Sinhala language into formatted editable text and describes how this system is integrated into an open-source word processing tool.
