Abstract Note: Nowadays AI, Robotics and Digital Technology have been implemented in hospitals and public places in relevance to social distancing, reducing one-to-one contact, enabling swift diagnosis, and sanitizing places during the COVID pandemic. As per its highly contagious nature of the coronavirus, various robots can deliver contact-free services in hospitals and public spaces as an alternative. Location-conscious computation includes the automatic customization of information and services that can be detected using low-cost robot. Robot can move through various areas as per the user's control. Low-cost robot can be used for the healthcare services of patients providing medicine and foods in the hospital and domestic purposes by rolling into treatment rooms, allowing health care workers to remotely measure parameters. In hospitals, the frontline workers, family members, and even receptionists can be remotely informed about patients in real-time. Specialized robots can handle additional works associated with a surge in patients, along with its regular activities. This robot may remotely transport infectious samples to laboratories for testing at specific distance. Current robot is controlled by a software application detecting the real-time need of the patients. Hence, the current robot could help the sustainable development concerned with clean and green technology. A route planning system-based programming that provides planning and implementation, initially preprocess, process, and then applied to physical robots as a post process and prototype, has been tested thus producing functional settings.
Notes: The study concerns a purpose-built healthcare robot and its software application, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: M. Pallot; R. Ruland; S. Traykov; K. Kristensen
Title: Integrating shared workspace, wiki and blog technologies to support interpersonal Knowledge Connection
Abstract Note: Nowadays, Concurrent Engineering generalised implementation within business and professional ecosystems requires new multidisciplinary and multi-site collaborative environments, methods and tools that could stimulate creativity and increase innovation opportunities. While the focus in the past was on how to improve processes within single organisations, the current business network dynamics render the old methods unusable. What is needed are the methods and tools to support interpersonal communication and interpersonal productivity in order to maintain a higher level of knowledge entropy that can eventually assist knowledge workers generating more ideas and therefore stimulates creativity. This paper presents a virtual space of networked individuals within on-line communities through the integration of several technologies, namely shared workspace, wikis, wikis and blogs, to better support interpersonal knowledge connection. While shared workspace technology has already been widely deployed to support project teams, very little has been done so far regarding the use of wiki and blog technologies in the context of supporting on-line communities (e.g. Wikipedia) of knowledge workers. Our main idea was to integrate those technologies together and to use the resulting collaborative environment as a knowledge networking instrument where fonnalised concepts and members' profile are key components to support people-concepts networking. Another aspect of this implementation is to be able to experiment new ways of connecting people and concepts together. There are already open source software components supporting hyper graph that could be used for navigating into people-concepts networks or maps where one can discover new relevant resources to collaborate with. This could lead to the design of a new open collaboration platfonn to stimulate creativity and innovation. The paper looks also into the open content licensing mode and its potential benefits into a collaborative working environment as a freedom element that spurs creativity and innovation. Overall, it is believed that this kind of technology integration could be providing much faster and broader access to existing knowledge and people knowhow, thus providing more opportunities or alternatives to professionals engaged into knowledge intensive work. Our approach is also to find a systematic way of collecting and analysing data in order to evaluate the impacts on interpersonal productivity, creativity and innovation within online collaboration sessions. After all, knowledge creation is a social activity that needs to be specifically addressed and supported within new collaborative working environments. The paper concludes by introducing a new scientific domain branded as "Knowledge Connection" which stands at the crossroads of existing scientific domains such as Knowledge Creation, Knowledge Representation and Visualisation, Collaborative Networks, and Computer Support for Collaborative Work.
Notes: The paper develops a collaborative knowledge-sharing environment and discusses creativity and productivity; OSS components are mentioned only as tools, with no study of OSS project lifecycle or maintenance.

Author: S. Garg; A. Balasubramanian; M. Puvvadi
Title: Agentic AI Foundations and Infrastructure for Scalable Multi-Agent System
Abstract Note: Large language models (LLMs) unite with multiagent systems (MAS) to create agentic AI systems which demonstrate autonomous behavior, persistent memory, advanced planning capabilities and collaborative tool usage. This research evaluates the essential elements required to support large-scale deployment of multi-agent LLM systems which need to be both dependable and maintainable as well as subject to governance. The paper follows the development from traditional MAS systems based on coordination, negotiation and formal protocols to current LLM-based agents which demonstrate collective intelligent behavior. We describe how LLM-based agent orchestration generates new infrastructure needs, which include diverse computing resources, standardized networks, adaptive memory systems, monitoring capabilities, and protection mechanisms. The research evaluates open-source platforms through architectural comparisons while identifying major scalability, sustainability and governance challenges. The survey creates infrastructure maps between compute resources, communication systems, storage needs and policy frameworks to direct future research and engineering development for next-generation agentic AI systems.
Notes: The paper presents a survey and architectural comparisons of existing platforms, rather than original empirical research.

Author: N. Kshetri
Title: From Challenges to Opportunities: Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Low-Resource Languages
Abstract Note: This article explores the role of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) in supporting low-resource languages (LRLs), spoken primarily by populations in developing economies, focusing on the challenges and solutions in creating language models for these contexts. It highlights the efforts of global institutions, governments, and the private sector in building sustainable AI ecosystems to empower speakers of LRLs.
Notes: The study concerns AI and language models for low-resource languages, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: N. A. Walee; A. Shalan; C. Kadlec; M. K. Rahman
Title: Optimizing Deep Learning Accuracy: Visibility Filtering Approach for Early Wildfire Detection in Forest Sensor Images
Abstract Note: Due to the destruction caused by wildfires underscores the critical need for proactive wildfire management strategies. Particularly, early detection of wildfires can mitigate their impact on the environment and economic loss and save human lives. This research study builds upon our prior work on refining and improving identifying early-stage wildfires. Previous research focused on using a deep-learning model for detecting early wildfires. This study aims to classify the visibility levels of forest sensory images to improve the deep learning model. Due to the constraints of existing public wildfire detection datasets, we have created a specialized forest sensory images dataset tailored specifically for detecting wildfires in their initial stages. We have used an Open-source computer vision library (OpenCV) for image processing integrated with TensorFlow and Keras to create a hybrid deep learning model. The results showed a significant improvement in the accuracy from 84% to 87% in detecting early spots of fire in images captured by surveillance cameras or/satellites. The Convolutional Neural Network model has been evaluated by crucial classification metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and f1 values. The study aids in progressing the efficacy of early wildfire detection, furnishing valuable perspectives for urban centers and nations contending with the dangers presented by these catastrophic natural events.
Notes: OpenCV is only a tool in a wildfire-detection study; the research does not examine OSS project lifecycle or abandonment-related concepts.

Author: C. Dacso; A. P. Dhawan
Title: Introducing the IEEE Journal of Translational Engineering in Health and Medicine
Abstract Note: The leadership at EMBS created the IEEE Journal of Translational Engineering in Health and Medicine (JTEHM) to address the critical need to disseminate innovative translational research in health and medicine. The journal's unique aim is to support the movement of biotechnological innovations from idea to clinical trials and commercialization. We intend for JTEHM to provide a vehicle for the consilience of engineering, medicine and health, and translation. Translation is the critical step to take technological advances from the lab into the clinical environment to improve clinical practice and healthcare. We chose the open-access route not because it is easier (it is not) but because it lays waste to the barrier of cost of reading. We are proud to introduce JTEHM with an open-source, continuous-publication platform that allows multimedia presentation of clinically significant translational technologies, along with editorial blogs and comments from experts, entrepreneurs and clinicians. The papers published in JTEHM are accessible through IEEE Xplore and will be in PubMed soon, as well as in downloadable PDF versions with additional material. We welcome submission of your research findings and clinical translation studies.
Notes: The title and abstract identify this as an introductory editorial for a journal, not an individual primary research study.

Author: T. Liu; L. Xie; H. Liu; R. Ye; H. Fan; L. Ding
Title: Multidimensional Matrix Profile-Based Anomaly Detection for Power Grid with High Variable Renewable Energy Penetration
Abstract Note: The development of various emerging artificial intelligence and big data technologies has gradually transformed traditional physical power systems into smart grids. With the high proportion of renewable energy connected to the grid in various countries becoming an irreversible trend, the increasingly frequent climate change has made data quality issues in transmission networks increasingly prominent. In order to ensure the safe operation of the power system, it is necessary to accurately and quickly detect and process abnormal data. This article comprehensively considers key issues in the field of multidimensional temporal anomaly detection and designs an anomaly detection method based on multidimensional Matrix Profile (MP) for real-time detection of multi-source heterogeneous data associated with transmission networks. It can extract key anomaly feature subsets from high-dimensional data and optimize window length selection in traditional MP methods. This article has been validated in open-source datasets and simulated synthetic power data. The experimental results show that the method based on multidimensional MP can effectively avoid the multi-parameter and data dependency problems of deep learning models, and has high scalability and flexibility.
Notes: The study develops anomaly detection for power-grid data; open-source datasets are only validation data, with no OSS lifecycle or abandonment-related focus.

Author: C. D. Montes; J. V. Silvosa; C. C. Abalorio; R. B. Nakazato
Title: Application of BERT Model for Unsupervised Text Classification using Hierarchical Clustering for Automatic Classification of Thesis Manuscript
Abstract Note: Many current studies on natural language processing (NLP) depend on supervised learning, which needs a lot of labeled data. This is not practical for large classification tasks. This research presents an unsupervised approach to automatically classify unlabeled theses using a BERT-hierarchical model. This technique combines BERT, an open-source machine-learning tool for NLP, with divisive hierarchical clustering utilizing the K-means clustering algorithm. Standard metrics evaluated the model's performance. Fine-tuning the BERT-hierarchical model with a learning rate of 0.00001 gave the best results, achieving 93% accuracy, 91% precision, and 93% recall. Additionally, a web application was created to facilitate model testing, offering functions for data creation, editing, and deletion. This study shows the BERT-hierarchical model's effectiveness in classifying unlabeled data, providing a scalable solution for large NLP tasks.
Notes: The study evaluates an NLP model for classifying theses; open-source BERT is only a tool, with no OSS project lifecycle or abandonment topic.

Author: N. Chothani; D. D. Patel
Title: Transmission Line Protection based on Fine-Tuning CatBoost Fault Classification Technique
Abstract Note: Transmission line challenges are complex because they involve many different factors and are subject to significant fluctuations. These complexities make it crucial to implement precise protective measures. Effective protection ensures that electrical power flows without interruption. To address these challenges, a new classification algorithm is proposed, which is based on CatBoost. This algorithm works in conjunction with a Wavelet Transform-based decomposition system. These tools help in accurately assessing the condition of the transmission lines and responding to any issues that may arise. For practical application, the Indian standard system serves as the simulation model. This system operates at a voltage rating of 220 kV and spans a length of 120 km, with a frequency of 50 Hz. The decomposition frequency is set at 4 kHz, and to perform the Wavelet decomposition method, 80 samples are taken per cycle. A comprehensive data collection occurs within the transmission line using the MULTIRUN block of PSCADTM software. This software is instrumental in gathering the necessary data for analysis. The developed CatBoost algorithm is implemented in MATLAB, ensuring that hyperparameters are optimized for better performance. Once data is collected from PSCADTM, it is then imported into MATLAB for further processing. The CatBoost algorithm is employed to validate the data and assess the performance of the transmission line protection system. The results from this classification reveal that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms traditional methods in protecting transmission lines.
Notes: The study concerns electrical transmission-line protection, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: U. R. Babu; N. Sharma; K. S. Kumar; D. D. Madhukar; P. R. Sonawane; N. Nishant
Title: IoT Based Environmental Monitoring System using LSTM-WAO-EEMD
Abstract Note: In this proposed approach, the system takes a look at the environmental monitoring systems that are based on the Internet of Things. The suggested system's primary function is to supply remote locations with environmental parameters via the internet. The proposed method is a practical and easy way to monitor the surrounding environment and atmosphere. The system is a representation of ambient and environmental parameter monitoring by use of low-power wireless sensors linked to the Internet that report their readings to a centralized server. Finally, data collected from all over the world may be seen on the base station remotely from any Internet-connected device. From the physical level, with its sensors and communication protocol, to the cyber level, with its data management and storage, this work comprises the full solution, a cyber-physical system. It solves the issue of incompatible systems by providing a clear structure for exchanging information between sensors of varying measuring capabilities. This improves the effectiveness of monitoring systems. Using real-time sensors, the suggested system monitors conditions like moisture, temperature, humidity, rainfall, gas concentration, and seismic notification. An open-source platform known as Thing speak checks in on these variables every 2 minutes. The sensor data is then preprocessed, the features are selected, and the model is trained. EEMD-WOA-LSTM is used in the proposed method. When compared to two other models, including LSTM and GRU, the suggested method fares exceptionally well.
Notes: The study proposes an IoT environmental-monitoring system using ThingSpeak as a platform; it does not investigate OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: A. A. Mohamed Nishar; A. Marefat; R. Sutradhar; N. Kabengi; P. Gore; B. Meyer; D. Dai; S. Andrews; X. He; A. Ashok
Title: Towards Modeling Underground Soil Radon Gas Emanation
Abstract Note: After cigarette smoking, Radon (222Rn) inhalation has been regarded the second most significant cause of lung cancer in the US and the world by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the World Health Organization (WHO). Radon is an inert noble radioactive gas produced by the Uranium (238U) decay series, specifically by the decay of Radium (226Ra) into Radon. Radon emanates naturally from the soil, particularly in regions rich in granite and slate. Thus far, there have been several controlled laboratory radioactive studies on the dependence of Radon gas emanation on atmospheric physical parameters such as humidity/moisture and temperature. However, there is no clear understanding of the exact emanation and transport process of Radon gas from the soil, and no model defines the dynamics. This paper presents our experience, learning, and modeling results from our extensive research on Radon emanation from soil. We consider a data-centric approach to modeling Radon emanation from the soil where we report and analyze data from a real-world underground Radon measurement testbed that we have installed on our site. In addition to presenting the testbed information, we report the results from evaluating ten of the most used and state-of-the-art supervised machine/deep learning time-series analysis models and unsupervised clustering analysis. We conclude this paper by summarizing our inferences and learning about our modeling results, the Radon modeling process, and the need for controlled lab experiments to validate and confirm on-field data-based analysis results. We plan to open the Radon testbed data used in this work to the public unon publication.
Notes: The study models radon emanation from soil using environmental measurements; its population and subject are not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: J. Paulos; P. R. Silva; R. J. Bessa; A. Marot; J. Dejaegher; B. Donnot
Title: Generation of Power Network Operating Scenarios for an AI-friendly Digital Environment
Abstract Note: With the growing need for AI-driven solutions in power grid management, this work addresses the challenge of creating realistic synthetic operating scenarios essential for developing, testing, and validating AI-based decision-making systems. It uses spatial-temporal noise functions, predefined patterns, and optimal power flow to model renewable energy and conventional power plant generation, load, and losses. Quantitative and visual key performance indicators are proposed to evaluate the quality of the generated operating scenarios, and the validation highlights the framework’s ability to emulate diverse and practical operating scenarios, bridging gaps in AI-driven power system research and real-world applications.
Notes: The study concerns power-network operating scenarios and AI-based power-system applications, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: N. Gandhi; L. Armstrong
Title: Applying data mining techniques to predict yield of rice in humid subtropical climatic zone of India
Abstract Note: Agricultural crop productivity depends on various factors such as precipitation, climate, soil type and hydrology. Statistical methods and techniques can be used to assess the impact of these factors on crop production. By applying these techniques on historical climate and crop production data it may provide knowledge which can be used by farmers or industry and government stakeholders for strategies which will lead to increased crop production. The present research focuses on application of data mining techniques to extract knowledge from the historical agricultural dataset to predict rice crop yield for Kharif season of Humid Subtropical climatic zone of India. The performance evaluation of different classification techniques has been carried out in free and open source data mining software WEKA (Waikato Environment for Knowledge Analysis) as part of this research on the agricultural dataset. The experimental result provided include sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, mean absolute error (MAE), root mean squared error (RMSE), relative absolute error (RAE) and root relative squared error (RRSE). The result on the current dataset shows that J48 and LADTree(Logical Analysis of Data Tree) classifiers provide the best performance of the classifiers used in this research.
Notes: The study predicts rice yield using agricultural data; WEKA is only the open-source analysis tool, and OSS lifecycle concepts are not studied.

Author: T. Dahlberg
Title: Keynote: A decade of broadening participation with STARS
Abstract Note: It has been ten years since we envisioned the STARS Alliance. We started as 10 Southeastern schools focused on regional partnerships and institutionalization of best practices, with specific focus on mentoring, high school outreach, research, and pair programming. Our intent was to build a vertical and horizontal community of “like” students that extends beyond the classroom walls. The field of computing has dramatically changed in the past decade, and so has STARS. We are now over 50 colleges and universities nationwide. We continue to effectively engage in mentoring, outreach and research — now augmenting these practices by invention, entrepreneurship, open source and an explosion in interdisciplinary applications for computer science. This talk is a retrospective of how STARS and best practices for broadening participation have changed, with suggestions for how best practices could evolve in the future.
Notes: The talk retrospectively discusses the STARS broadening-participation community; open source is mentioned as one activity, with no study of OSS project lifecycle or maintenance.

Author: U. Zanovello; A. Arduino; V. Basso; L. Zilberti; A. Sola; A. Agosto; L. Toso; O. Bottauscio
Title: Very-Low-Field MRI Scanners: From the Ideal to the Real Permanent Magnet Array
Abstract Note: Very-low-field (VLF) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is becoming increasingly popular due to its portability and adaptability to different environments. They are being successfully used for various clinical applications, leading to a paradigm shift in the way imaging care is typically performed. The development of low-cost MRI scanner prototypes began a few years ago, with some interesting and promising open-source projects emerging in both hardware and software design. Using permanent magnets (PMs) to generate the static magnetic field  $B_{0}$  can substantially reduce the manufacturing cost while achieving satisfactory homogeneity. This article aims to explore the reasons behind discrepancies between magnet design and prototype performance in terms of magnetic field homogeneity. Understanding the impact of the practical implementation of magnet design could inform the development of more tolerant designs in the future, simplifying subsequent  $B_{0}$  shimming procedures or even making them unnecessary. This work also evidences the impact of using different numerical model approximations in the modeling phase, proving how they also impact the quality of the design outcomes.
Notes: The study concerns MRI magnet design and prototype performance; open-source projects are mentioned only as context, not studied as software projects or their lifecycle.

Author: B. Hyseni; L. A. Bexheti
Title: Perspective of open data application in Kosovo, challenges, and advantages
Abstract Note: Purpose of the research: the research aimed to measure the perspective of Open Data application in Kosovo, based on the current conditions of use of Open Data, the challenges they face, as well as the advantages offered through Open Data. Methods: the focus of the research is the public institutions of the Republic of Kosovo, respectively the research was conducted through the analysis of the strategy of application of open data, the survey of experts in the field, officials of public institutions, and other professionals. The research was conducted in January and February 2022. The research belongs to the quantitative type through the analysis of the legal document and the interviews represent the high -level aspect, while through the survey the opinion of experts and applicants of public institutions for the application of Open Data in the Republic of Kosovo. Results: The data were qualitatively processed through the qualitative method of interpretation, while the survey data were processed through the SPSS program using the SEM Structural Equation Model method and factor analysis. Based on the research, some recommendations for institutions and challenges to the application of open data in Kosovo have been identified. Conclusion and recommendation: according to the research results I conclude that the advantages of Open Data application in Kosovo are related to data optimization and external access, its synchronization, improvement of values in economic and policymaking, development of knowledge, and reliability of investments. loans in the Republic of Kosovo, while the challenges are the regulation of privacy and copyright, information source, their standardization, and a joint Open Data portal for public data. Through this research, I manage to provide a clear overview of the Open Data application which requires the drafting of Open Data application standards in Kosovo, an aspect that regulates all forms of Open Data application. Scientific effects: the scientific impact of the research lies in the regulation of state strategies and the standardization and improvement of the Open Data application at the state level of the Republic of Kosovo.
Notes: The study examines open data application by Kosovo public institutions, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: S. G. Quansah; W. A. Nettey; H. Afeku-Amenyo; P. Lal
Title: Geospatial Cyber-Physical Risk Assessment of Critical Energy Infrastructure in Essex County, New Jersey
Abstract Note: As New Jersey advances towards its 2035 clean energy goal, a critical gap remains in identifying where cyber-physical threats to the grid are most likely to trigger high-impact disruptions. This study addresses the question: where in Essex County do cyber exposure, flood risk, and social vulnerability converge to create high-priority zones for infrastructure hardening? We develop a GIS-based multi-criteria risk model using publicly available data sources including census tract boundaries from NJOGIS and the U.S. Census Bureau, internet-exposed Industrial Control System (ICS) devices identified via Shodan passive scanning, FEMA Digital Flood Insurance Rate Maps, and CDC Social Vulnerability Index data at the census-tract level. Risk scores are generated via weighted linear combination with equal weights applied to each component (33% each) to provide a balanced, transparent assessment. Preliminary analysis reveals exposed ICS devices concentrated in Newark and elevated social vulnerability scores in 62% of Essex County tracts, suggesting non-trivial spatial overlap of vulnerability factors. Final outputs include a composite risk map and statistically significant hotspots identified via Moran’s I spatial autocorrelation and Getis-Ord Gi* analysis. This work demonstrates how open-source geospatial analytics can bridge academic research, utility operations, and state energy policy, enhancing grid resilience where it matters most.
Notes: The study examines energy infrastructure and cyber-physical risks, not OSS projects or ecosystems; open-source geospatial analytics are only a tool.

Author: M. Cenk; A. Malhotra; J. A. Akinyele
Title: Confidential Transfers for Multi-Purpose Tokens on the XRP Ledger
Abstract Note: We introduce Confidential Transfers for Multi-Purpose Tokens (Confidential MPTs) on the XRP Ledger, a cryptographic extension of the XLS-33 token standard that enables confidential balances and hidden transfer amounts while preserving public supply verifiability. The protocol replaces plaintext per-account balances with EC–ElGamal ciphertexts and employs non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs to enforce transfer correctness, balance sufficiency, and the invariant OutstandingAmount  $\leq $  MaxAmount without requiring decryption by validators. Confidentiality is scoped to transaction amounts and account balances; sender and receiver identities remain public, preserving XRPL’s account-based execution model. Our design maintains full compatibility with existing MPT semantics: public and confidential balances coexist, issuance rules remain unchanged, and the issuer’s designated second account is treated identically to other holders. The protocol further supports issuer-controlled operations, including freeze and clawback, without weakening supply soundness. To accommodate regulatory and institutional requirements, Confidential MPTs provide cryptographic auditability through an on-chain selective-disclosure model based on multi-ciphertext balance representations and equality proofs, while remaining compatible with simpler issuer-mediated audit models. We present a complete protocol specification, a security analysis under standard discrete-logarithm assumptions, and an open-source reference implementation (mpt-crypto) that realizes the required cryptographic primitives. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that confidential transfers can be verified within XRPL validator performance constraints, with proof sizes and verification costs suitable for production deployment.
Notes: The study develops and evaluates a confidential-token protocol; the open-source implementation is incidental, with no investigation of OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: F. D. Olana; B. Á. Turóczi; Z. Amri; B. Bereczki; J. Kiss; B. Hartmann
Title: Exploration of Multi-Timescale and Multi-Granularity Power System Models: A Literature Review and the Case Study of a Transmission System Operator
Abstract Note: This paper provides a structured review of electric power system modelling approaches across multiple time scales, ranging from short-term electromagnetic transients to long-term steady state behaviour. With the growing use of renewable energy like solar and wind, distributed generation, and complex system dynamics, accurately modelling power systems has become both critical and challenging. The literature review is organized by time scale to highlight specific methods, tools, and their gaps. Key issues include limited real-world validation, a lack of unified frameworks, challenges in capturing renewable variability, and high computational demands. Emerging techniques such as co-simulation and adaptive methods are discussed as potential solutions. The review emphasizes the need for integrated modelling strategies that balance accuracy, complexity, and practical applicability for future power system studies. The second part of the paper takes the opposite viewpoint and provides insight of the toolset of an actual transmission system operator. The comparison underlines that while multi-timescale and multi-granularity modelling is a key issue in the research community, the need for such tools from industrial users is less clearly identifiable.
Notes: The study reviews electric power system models and a transmission system operator’s tools, not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: S. Matheswaran; P. V. D. Vamsi; M. D. Chowdary; U. Allimuthu; C. E. Singh
Title: Design and Evaluation of a Trace-Driven Cache Simulator Supporting Set-Associative and V-Way Cache Architectures
Abstract Note: Modern processors increasingly suffer from cache due to conflict misses arising from the rigid placement constraints imposed. By conventional set-associative cache architectures. Although Advanced designs such as the V-Way cache improve place ment flexibility through decoupled tag-data storage and in increased effective associativity, practical tools for studying their Alternative behaviors are considerably limited in their application. This paper presents a Light weight, open-source, trace-driven cache simulator supporting both classical setassociative caches as well as the V-Way cache architecture. Author: A. Negi; P. Gupta; R. Pradhan
Title: Retraction Notice: Artificial Intelligence for Cancer Diagnosis and Prognosis: Current Status and Future Directions
Abstract Note: The medical field and public health care has achieved radical progress in the last age, the original reasons behind abundant conditions were disclosed, novel symptomatic forms were devised, and new cures were developed. The second leading cause of death is cancer. worldwide afflicting approximately six out of every ten people. Variants of the lungs and colon of all cancers are those that prevalent and most fatal. However, detecting the disease in its infancy increases the odds of survival dramatically. Over the last three decades, the number of cancer victims and the scope of cancer survivability research has increased. This chapter provides a review of all types of cancer prediction with interventional and observational cancer survivorship research efforts. The treatment of cancer type is increasingly required in early cancer research. The advancement of healthcare research has been boosted by artificial intelligence. Researchers have developed program to help cancer identification and prognosis due to the availability of open-source healthcare statistics. In these conditions, DL and ML models give a dependable, quick, and effective method for dealing with such difficult diseases. Cancer categorization is a contentious issue in medicine since it allows for precise and effective diagnosis and promotes a favorable outcome in medical therapies.
Notes: The record concerns cancer diagnosis and prognosis using AI; open-source statistics are only a data resource, with no OSS lifecycle or abandonment topic studied.

Author: Z. Zheng; Z. Y. Dong; G. Chen; Y. Tao; E. Su; S. Lai; Z. Huang; T. Li; X. Jiang
Title: Operator Splitting Scheme Based Distributed Energy Management for Networked Multi-Microgrids
Abstract Note: Efficient and coordinated management of networked multi-microgrid systems is crucial, especially in background of energy structure transition and wide deployment of distributed renewable energy sources. To address the energy management challenges of these systems, this paper proposes a novel distributed framework. The framework requires only communication between neighboring microgrids to realize local computation, which effectively maintains the autonomous decision-making capability of each microgrid. By abandoning centralized data aggregation, the approach guarantees data privacy and local operational decision independence. A rigorous derivation constructed based on operator splitting theory proves that the distributed framework can converge to the optimal solution of the problem when the local step-size condition is satisfied. Simulation results further verify the convergence and effectiveness of the framework.
Notes: The study concerns energy management in networked microgrids, not OSS projects or repositories.

Author: R. K. K; S. M. U. Sankar; D. K. S; D. K. A; D. A
Title: A Multi-Layered Cyber Security and Analytics Framework for Tokenized, Transaction-Linked WIFI Authentication in Business
Abstract Note: Public and shared Wi-Fi networks often allow unrestricted internet access once a device connects, creating security risks, misuse of bandwidth, and a lack of user accountability. To tackle these issues, this paper presents the design and implementation of a QR code-based captive portal system for secure and time-controlled Wi-Fi access using the pfSense firewall platform The proposed system blocks internet connectivity until users finishes an authentication process through a captive portal interface. The system is set up in a virtualized environment using VMware, where pfSense works as the main firewall and routing gateway. A captive portal is enabled on the local network to intercept user traffic and redirect unauthenticated devices to a custom login page. The login interface shows a dynamically generated QR code, which users scan to start authentication. A backend server checks the QR request and communicates with pfSense to approve the session. Once verified successfully, internet access is granted for a set period, after which the session automatically ends. Experimental evaluation with multiple client devices shows that the system effectively blocks unauthorized access, enforces time-based connectivity, and ensures users are redirected to the captive portal after their session expires. This approach provides a practical, scalable, and cost-effective solution for managing Wi-Fi access in settings like educational institutions, public networks, and small businesses.
Notes: The study evaluates a Wi-Fi captive-portal authentication system; OSS is not the lifecycle subject, and no abandonment-related concept is investigated.

Author: K. Sathesh; G. V. Kumar; J. V. Vardhan; P. V. Vamsi; P. Chittipolu; V. Nagaraja
Title: Design and Physical Implementation of an RV32IM RISC-V Core in 7-nm Technology Using Cadence EDA Flow
Abstract Note: This paper presents an end-to-end ASIC design flow for implementing an RV32IM RISC-V CPU core using industry-standard Cadence EDA tools in a 7 nm technology node. The objective is to demonstrate a complete and realistic VLSI design methodology, covering the entire flow from RTL design to final physical implementation. Functional verification is first carried out using Cadence NCLaunch and SimVision by monitoring key signals such as the program counter, instruction fields, operands, and ALU outputs. The verified RTL is then synthesized using Cadence Genus under timing constraints to generate the netlist and analyze area, power, and timing metrics. Subsequently, physical design is performed in Cadence Innovus, including die and core planning, power ring and strap creation, standard cell placement, routing, and clock tree synthesis. Clock tree synthesis ensures balanced clock skew and insertion delay for synchronous operation. Finally, global and detailed routing across multiple metal layers achieves a dense interconnect layout within core boundaries. This work bridges the gap between academic RTL design and practical ASIC implementation, demonstrating the feasibility of deploying open-source RISC-V cores in deep submicron, low-power SoC applications.
Notes: The study presents an ASIC implementation flow for an open-source RISC-V core; it does not investigate the core’s abandonment, maintenance, activity, or lifecycle.

Author: R. Alhajj
Title: ASONAM 2013 message from steering chair
Abstract Note: This is the first time the ASONAM conference has been organized in North America. I am so delighted to watch the conference moving up so fast with consistent and hopefully sustainable success. Achieving acceptance rate of 13% this year is a new record which brings a challenge for the new organizers. I am sure they are aware of the mission and will be able to maintain the same quality for the coming years. We need to show the success as permanent for ASONAM to continue its mission as the leading venue in the area of social networks analysis and mining. The number of quality submissions is rapidly increasing every year demonstrating the visibility of the conference and making it harder to select the papers to accommodate in the program. The quality of workshops co-located with ASONAM has been considerably improved this year. In addition, I am happy to witness the success of the two symposiums which have been integrated into the organization to have more specialized coverage of two key areas related to network based modeling and analysis. The symposium on the Foundations of Open Source Intelligence and Security Informatics (FOSINT-SI) is serving mostly researchers and practitioners interested in terror and criminal data analysis. On the other hand, the symposium on Network Enabled Health Informatics, Biomedicine and Bioinformatics (HI-BI-BI) covers the network applications in the health domain from the wet-lab to the clinic.

Author: Mariel Borowitz
Title: 6 Group on Earth Observations
Abstract Note: The Group on Earth Observations (GEO) was formed in 2005, with promotion of full and open data sharing as one of its primary goals. GEO grew out of a desire to improve international cooperation on collection and sharing of environmental data for a wide range of environmental issues, rather than focusing on one domain, such as weather or climate. While it requires high-level political participation, the organization was formed as a stand-alone international body, not affiliated with the United Nations or another group, and its policies and plans are considered nonbinding on its members. This structure has given GEO the flexibility to continually advocate for forward-looking data sharing principles and to push its members to adopt increasingly open policies. In its first ten years, GEO has been an important venue for international debates on data sharing and for exchanging information about the impact of various data policy choices.
Notes: The study concerns an international organization and environmental data-sharing policies, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: F. Adesola; O. Adeyinka; A. Kayode; A. Ayodele
Title: Implementation of Multi-modal Speech Emotion Recognition Using Text Data and Audio Signals
Abstract Note: Speech emotion detection is a difficult task, and models that employ audio characteristics in developing high-performing classifiers have received much attention in recent times. The effectiveness of emotional features extracted from speech has a significant impact on Speech Emotion Recognition's (SER) performance. On the other hand, most emotional features are sensitive to non-emotional factors such as the speaker, speaking styles, and environment. A deep dual recurrent encoder model is developed in this research. It sequentially uses text data and audio signals to comprehend speech data better and categorise it using various labels such as happy, sad, neutral, and angry. While emotional interaction comprises sound and speech, this model uses dual Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to encode information from audio and text sequences and then integrate it to predict the emotion class. This architecture analyses audio signals from the signal to the language level, allowing it to use the data's information than models that only focus on audio characteristics. The model is further presented via a web application that recognises emotion from recorded spoken utterances. Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) and Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) are used to create the front-end components. On the other hand, the backend components are built with Django, SQLite as database, and Docker containers. TensorFlow, an open-source software framework for machine learning and deep neural networks were also used to create the model. Categorising utterances into one of four emotion categories, the model used on the USC-IEMOCAP dataset had an accuracy of 68.26%. This model has increasingly broadened its applications because it is an essential component of optimal human-computer interactions, such as dialogue systems.
Notes: The study develops a speech-emotion recognition model; open-source software is mentioned only as a tool, with no OSS lifecycle or abandonment-related subject.

Author: R. Alhajj
Title: ASONAM 2014 message from steering chair
Abstract Note: Three years past since the ASONAM conference was held in Asia for the first time. ASONAM is organized in Beijing this year as part of the trend to rotate the location between North America, Europe and Asia. Many developments and great achievements have been witnessed during the past three years. The size of the conference has grown more than double its size in Taiwan three years ago. In addition to the workshops which have been organized with ASONAM since it started in 2009 in Athens, Greece, the conference has expanded to include tutorials, demos, industrial track and a panel. Also two symposiums very related to the scope of ASONAM are now constantly organized in conjunction with ASONAM and rapidly growing. The symposium on the Foundations of Open Source Intelligence and Security Informatics (FOSINT-SI) is serving mostly researchers and practitioners interested in terror and criminal data analysis. On the other hand, the symposium on Network Enabled Health Informatics, Biomedicine and Bioinformatics (HI-BI-BI) covers the network applications in the health domain from the wet-lab to the clinic. Further, ASONAM is returning to Asia as a financially sponsored venue jointly by the two leading computing organizations, namely IEEE Computer Society and ACM. More important is maintaining the high quality of the papers presented in three parallel sessions for three full days. The acceptance rate has been always kept below 20% and this year it is almost 18%. Indeed, the number of quality submissions is rapidly increasing every year demonstrating the visibility of the conference and making it harder to select the papers to accommodate in the program. Also, the quality of workshops co-located with ASONAM has been considerably improved this year. I know that some researchers hesitate to submit to ASONAM due to this lower acceptance rate. I strongly encourage researchers to continue to submit their high quality papers to ASONAM for several reasons. ASONAM is characterized by consistent and sustainable success. It is the flagship and premier venue where distinguished researcher and practitioners get together to discuss latest developments as well as the vision for future developments and research directions in the area of social networks analysis and mining. Presenting a paper at ASONAM is a privilege because we try our best to keep the review and decision processes based merely on the quality of the submissions and only best papers are selected for inclusion in the program. Presenting at ASONAM will allow researchers to meet, discuss their research, and receive feedback from internationally recognized researchers in the field. Every year, authors of all the papers presented at ASONAM are invited to submit expanded versions of their manuscripts to the prestigious SNAM journal or the LNSN series which are characterized by their high visibility and fast processing of the submissions.

Author: R. Kumar; S. Gupta; Y. Srivastava; H. Srivastava
Title: AI Assisted Plant Disease Detection, Crop And Fertilizer Recommendation System
Abstract Note: Agriculture is a cornerstone of India's economy, employing nearly half of its population and contributing significantly to its growth. Understanding the importance of nutrient management for crop productivity is paramount. However, Indian farmers face formidable challenges, including unpredictable irrigation patterns and poor soil quality, often lacking the necessary knowledge and resources for informed decision-making in crop selection and fertilizer use. Crop failures have profound consequences, affecting livelihoods and food security, while also posing risks to the environment. To address these challenges, our research presents an innovative solution in the form of an open-source, user-friendly web application. This application offers support for crop and fertilizer recommendations, a forecast of plant diseases, and an interactive news stream. Additionally, our approach incorporates interpretability techniques to elucidate predictions made by our disease detection model, making it a comprehensive tool for farmers and stakeholders in the agricultural sector. Our research endeavors to provide a practical and efficient solution to enhance crop production, thereby contributing to the sustainable development of India's agriculture and economy.
Notes: The study presents an open-source agricultural decision-support application; it does not investigate OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: R. H. Shihab; T. H. Zihan; J. Mollick; B. R. Arif; M. Hasan; M. T. Habib
Title: A Scalable IoMT Platform for Unified Medical Device Monitoring in Resource-Constrained Environments
Abstract Note: Smart healthcare systems in low-resource areas typically do not have a unified system, rather they have separate IoT dashboards. This makes it difficult for caregivers to see the full picture of the patient's condition as they rely on paper based static reports. To solve this problem, This paper presents an integrated Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) platform that integrates two neonatal devices, a Vital Sign Monitor (VSM) and a Phototherapy Light (PTL). The proposed system uses Node-RED for edge data ingestion, an MQTT based communication layer, and a hybrid database backend (MongoDB for time-series sensor data and MySQL for structured information). It includes a web dashboard for real-time monitoring of neonates, and WhatsApp based alerts for critical events. We outline important design patterns (flow based Node-RED routing, lightweight on edge rule evaluation) that allow for rapid development and flexibility. In our tests, the system achieved an end-to-end delay of under 100 ms and showed zero data loss at regular workloads. In a mock deployment, clinicians responded faster to emergencies after receiving WhatsApp alerts. This denotes, this method is practical and more adaptable for hospitals in low- and middle-income countries.
Notes: The study concerns a purpose-built healthcare IoMT platform, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: S. B. Ehsan; A. Majumder; M. A. Razzaque; K. M. S. Nomani; M. S. Islam; M. S. Hossain
Title: DDoS Attack Detection for Network and Transport Layer using SIEM for Deeper Analysis
Abstract Note: The Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks have been recognized as the most disruptive threat in cybersecurity, where the attacker produces a large amount of malicious traffic to the victim’s network to make the system unavailable. DDoS attack mitigation is quite challenging due to IP spoofing, large traffic volume, and protocol exploitation in the network and transport layers. Our aim is to design a low-cost solution using open-source tools with deeper visualization, flexibility, and scalability, which are limited in most existing studies. In this paper, we have proposed a SIEM-based (Security Information and Event Management) architecture for the early detection of DDoS attacks to reduce the impact of service disruptions. We have incorporated important components such as Suricata (IDS), SIEM, and the Kibana Dashboard in this architecture. We have also analyzed the Kibana Dashboard with SIEM, which acts as a key feature for performance evaluation indicators. Using this method, we achieved a more insightful outcome for the detection of DDoS attacks on Layer 3 and Layer 4 of the OSI model.
Notes: Open-source tools are used to build a DDoS detection architecture; the study does not examine OSS project lifecycle or maintenance.

Title: SEED inauguration workshop: Building a digital ecosystem for societal empowerment
Abstract Note: Summary form only given. We are bringing together some leading researchers and practitioners in the field of sustainable development as “Experts on Tap” to both seed and guide this conversationally-based workshop. Traditional approaches to Social, Economic and Environmental Development (SEED) have historically employed a closed, top-down model in which problems are viewed narrowly and the input of local stakeholders is rarely sought. More recent efforts to address development from a holistic, multidisciplinary perspective—while a major step in the right direction—have been hindered by a lack of appropriate tools and well-defined processes to enable disparate resources to work effectively together towards common goals. The SEED Framework, developed by iFOSSF (International Free and Open Source Solutions Foundation), is specifically designed to support locally-led innovation with self-organizing, multidisciplinary collaborations and, most importantly, to translate concepts and ideas into actions. Combining the strength of both structured and unstructured workforces, the framework employs an open, “coopetition” strategy that integrates existing standards and practices across multiple sectors, enabling a high-level, results-oriented collaboration with a deep awareness of the local culture. The key components of the SEED Framework neatly dovetail with many existing DEST2013 tracks and the model provides an exciting and unprecedented opportunity to integrate participants’ individual contributions within a greater whole.
Notes: The workshop concerns a framework for sustainable development and societal collaboration; OSS is mentioned as the framework’s origin, not studied as a project lifecycle or maintenance topic.

Author: M. V. R. Malladi; N. Chebrolu; I. Scacchetti; L. Lobefaro; T. Guadagnino; B. Casseau; H. Oh; L. Freißmuth; M. Karppinen; J. Schweier; S. Leutenegger; J. Behley; C. Stachniss; M. Fallon
Title: Digiforests: a Longitudinal Lidar Dataset for Forestry Robotics
Abstract Note: Forests are vital to our ecosystems, acting as carbon sinks, climate stabilizers, biodiversity centers, and wood sources. Due to their scale, monitoring and managing forests takes a lot of work. Forestry robotics offers the potential for enabling efficient and sustainable foresting practices through automation. Despite increasing interest in this field, the scarcity of robotics datasets and benchmarks in forest environments is hampering progress in this domain. In this paper, we present a real-world, longitudinal dataset for forestry robotics that enables the development and comparison of approaches for various relevant applications, ranging from semantic interpretation to estimating traits relevant to forestry management. The dataset consists of multiple recordings of the same plots in a forest in Switzerland during three different growth periods. We recorded the data with a mobile 3D LiDAR scanning setup. Additionally, we provide semantic annotations of trees, shrubs, and ground, instance-level annotations of trees, as well as more fine-grained annotations of tree stems and crowns. Furthermore, we provide reference field measurements of traits relevant to forestry management for a subset of the trees. Together with the data, we also provide open-source baseline panoptic segmentation and tree trait estimation approaches to enable the community to bootstrap further research and simplify comparisons in this domain.
Notes: The study concerns a forestry robotics dataset and its applications; open-source baseline approaches are provided, but OSS projects are not the study population or subject.

Author: T. Motshegwa; C. Wright; H. Sithole; C. Ngolwe; A. Morgan
Title: Developing a Cyber-infrastructure for Enhancing Regional Collaboration on Education, Research, Science, Technology and Innovation
Abstract Note: This paper discusses the development of the Southern African Development Community shared cyber-infrastructure. The cyber-infrastructure aims to entrench regional integration through collaboration around education, research & development and innovation to address data and computationally intensive problems of regional significance and impact. It aims to achieve this by developing computational and data infrastructure, promoting research data sharing, pooling expertise and resources and consolidation through Centers of Excellence. The cyber-infrastructure is developed through a SADC Framework instrument that defined strategic goals and objectives and the components of the cyber-infrastructure. Furthermore, focus areas of resourcing, an implementation mechanism, the requisite policy framework, governance structures were defined together with resource mobilisation strategies and the necessary monitoring & evaluation reporting instruments.
Notes: The study concerns regional cyber-infrastructure for education and research, not OSS projects, repositories, or ecosystems.

Author: S. Depuru; N. Chandana; P. Alekhya; S. Madhu; S. V. C. Devi
Title: LLM-based Security Audit Assistant for Configuration File Analysis
Abstract Note: The increasing adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) in cybersecurity opens up promising avenues for automating the detection of misconfigurations in system and application configuration files. In this work, we present an LLM-Based Security Audit Assistant that integrates conventional rule-based validation with the contextual reasoning capability of LLMs. The system supports multiple configuration formats, performs early secret detection and redaction, and leverages retrieval-augmented prompts to deliver targeted remediation steps. To test the methodology, we created a collection of 4,200 configuration artifacts from open-source projects, enterprise applications, and emulated cloud environments, spanning YAML, JSON, XML, INI, and Docker Compose formats. Experimental results demonstrate that our suggested hybrid model attains 97.1% precision and 95.6% recall with 3.1% false positives, which outperforms rule-only and LLM-only baselines. The solution could be deployed in real time within CI/CD pipelines because the average processing latency was less than 150 ms per file. These results show that a practical path to precise and scalable configuration file security auditing is to combine deterministic tests with LLM-driven reasoning.
Notes: The study evaluates configuration-file security auditing; open-source projects are only one source of artifacts, with no investigation of project lifecycle or maintenance.

Author: H. Ariza; J. C. Martinez-Santos; E. D. Payares; M. F. Medina; J. A. Dominguez-Jimenez; J. Campillo
Title: A Blockchain Solution for Operational Parameters Monitoring Platform for DC Microgrids
Abstract Note: Large penetration of renewable distributed energy resources, as well as the effective integration of storage systems and electric vehicles, are some of the required strategies to reduce the impact of the energy sector on greenhouse gas emissions. Microgrids offer an efficient platform to facilitate the integration of these systems, however, the increased complexity this strategy comes with, requires the use of sophisticated, reliable, and secure monitoring and control systems. The outbreak of cryptocurrency technologies has drawn particular attention, especially, the underlying Blockchain technology. The decentralized structure of this technology enables implementing control strategies, parameters monitoring, and business processes in microgrids. The aim of this work is to present the development of a framework to monitor operational parameters from an islanded microgrid. To build the Blockchain network, the Hyperledger-Fabric development platform was used. To simulate the behavior of the microgrid, an object-oriented open-source library using the Modelica modeling language was used to model a DC microgrid. The performance of the architecture was evaluated through operational parameters such as the difficulty and the number of nodes. Results suggest that changes in these factors can affect significantly the transaction time. The proposed architecture can be used as a basis to study Blockchain communication effects in smart grids and their development.
Notes: The study develops and evaluates a blockchain monitoring framework for microgrids; open-source software is only a simulation tool, with no OSS lifecycle or abandonment-related subject.

Author: Q. Zheng; H. He; T. Ma; N. Xue; B. Li; B. Dong
Title: Big Log Analysis for E-Learning Ecosystem
Abstract Note: Recently, e-Learning emerges a rapid development, and e-Learning ecosystem has been proposed to provide sustained and stable services to cope with the growing demands of e-Learning. In e-Learning ecosystem, the amount of e-Learning log grows exponentially, introducing the variety and complexity of e-Learning log analysis. Therefore, a robust, scalable and practical logging architecture is urgently needed. Firstly, the characteristics of e-Learning log and its analysis are studied in this paper. Specifically, e-Learning log implies complicated characteristics, such as multi-dimensional correlation, heterogeneous multi-source, and cascading generation. Furthermore, the log analysis represents abundant diversity of demands, variety of methods and low-latency requirement in computation. Thereupon, this study presents a comprehensive logging architecture covering the whole life cycle of e-Learning log data which includes log collection, transport, storage, computation and service. To verify the proposed logging architecture, a related experimental implementation is developed for a realistic e-Learning ecosystem, and three typical e-Learning analyses are proposed.
Notes: The study develops a logging architecture for e-learning data; OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment is not investigated.

Author: N. H; R. K; S. M; T. Tsering; V. V
Title: A Review of Advancements in NLP and Speech Recognition for Enhanced Operating Systems
Abstract Note: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into operating systems is revolutionising user interaction by enhancing functionality and accessibility, particularly through technologies like Natural Language Processing (NLP) and speech recognition. Linux, with its open-source flexibility, has become a preferred platform for developing AI-driven solutions, enabling seamless adaptation and innovation in AI applications. This research study analyses the implementation of NLP and speech recognition in Linux environments, focusing on their impact on human-computer interaction and overall system usability. This study also highlights the technical challenges, such as maintaining privacy, addressing security risks, and ensuring system efficiency, particularly in diverse and resource-limited environments. While AI offers transformative potential in operating systems, this research study highlights the importance of addressing ethical concerns and maintaining robust governance to ensure user privacy and trust. Through responsible development, AI-enhanced systems can offer significant improvements in user experience while mitigating associated risks.
Notes: The study reviews AI/NLP and speech-recognition implementation in Linux for usability and technical challenges, not OSS project lifecycle or abandonment-related concerns.

Author: J. M. Peñaranda; M. C. Pacis
Title: Stochastic Optimal Transmission Switching Considering Voltage Stability Index with Distributed Generation Uncertainty
Abstract Note: Optimal Transmission Switching (OTS) is a strategic way of removing or connecting a transmission line to alter the network topology to optimize an objective such as cost reduction and power loss minimization. A deterministic optimization model and a DCOTS solution were utilized in earlier investigations of OTS. However, the uncertainty induced by the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources in the system must not be neglected, while inaccuracy lies in the DCOTS solution. Also, the voltage collapse point of the transmission line must be considered without sacrificing the system’s reliability. Hence, this research study aims to assess the impact of reducing the Expected Total Generation Cost (ETGC) using Stochastic AC Optimal Transmission Switching on the reliability and voltage stability of the power system with distributed generation uncertainty. The result of the study shows that Stochastic ACOTS reduced the expected generation cost by 2.19% for low demand, 7.03% for high demand, and 7.15% for very-high demand. Furthermore, in terms of the voltage stability index-LSI, ETGC savings due to OTS action have a low positive link with LSImax reduction. Then, the result shows that removing the top candidate line will not compromise the line stability index since the maximum LSI for low demand is 0.534, 0.696 for high demand, and 0.743 for very-high demand. Lastly, the proposed three-stage Stochastic ACOTS that ranks the line for removal shows that removing top candidate lines for all power demand levels does not produce immense Expected Demand Not Supplied (EDNS), which reveals the system’s reliability is not compromised. The optimization framework used in this study is the Python Optimization Model (Pyomo) while utilizing the open-source software IPOPT as the solver for non-linear problems.
Notes: The study concerns power-system transmission switching and reliability; IPOPT is only an open-source solver, not the OSS project or lifecycle under study.

Author: P. Wadhwa; K. Thielemans; N. Efthimiou; O. Bertolli; E. Emond; B. A. Thomas; M. Tohme; K. A. Wangerin; G. Delso; W. Hallett; R. N. Gunn; D. Buckley; C. Tsoumpas
Title: Implementation of Image Reconstruction for GE SIGNA PET/MR PET Data in the STIR Library
Abstract Note: Software for Tomographic Image Reconstruction (STIR: http://stir.sf.net) is an open source C++ library available for reconstruction of emission tomography data. This work aims at the incorporation of the GE SIGNA PET/MR scanner in STIR and enables PET image reconstruction with data corrections. The data extracted from the scanner after an acquisition includes a list of raw data files (emission, normalisation, geometric and well counter calibration (wcc) factors), magnetic resonance attenuation correction (MRAC) images and the scanner-based reconstructions. The listmode (LM) file stores a list of 'prompt' events and the singles per crystal per second. MRAC images from the scanner are used for attenuation correction. The modifications to STIR that allow accurate histogramming of this LM data in the same sinogram organisation as the scanner are also described. This allows reconstruction of acquisition data with all data corrections using STIR, and independent of any software supplied by the manufacturer. The implementations were validated by comparing the histogrammed data, data corrections and final reconstruction using the ordered subset expectation maximisation (OSEM) algorithm with the equivalents from the GE-toolbox, supplied by the manufacturer for the scanner. There is no difference in the histogrammed counts whereas an overall relative difference of 6.7 × 10-8% and from 0.01% to 0.86% is seen in the normalisation and randoms correction sinograms respectively. The STIR reconstructed images have similar resolution and quantification but have some residual differences due to wcc factors, decay and deadtime corrections, as well as the offset between PET and MR gantries that will be addressed in future work. This work will enable the use of all current and future STIR algorithms, including penalized image reconstruction, motion correction and direct parametric image estimation, on data from GE SIGNA PET/MR scanners.
Notes: The study develops and validates PET image-reconstruction functionality in an open-source library; it does not investigate OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment.

Author: A. Giri; A. S. M. A. S. Akib; A. Z. M. J. Uddin; M. S. Rahman; A. Hasib; M. Khadgi; M. F. Ferdous; M. Giri; B. Shahi
Title: EduBot: A Low-Cost Multilingual AI Educational Robot for Inclusive and Scalable Learning
Abstract Note: This paper presents EduBot, a novel, low-cost, AIpowered educational robot designed to foster inclusive and scalable learning for Bangla and English-speaking communities. EduBot addresses critical limitations in existing educational robotics-high cost, restricted language support, and lack of contextual adaptability-by integrating multilingual interaction, Optical Character Recognition (OCR), speech recognition, face detection, and deep learning-based natural language processing within a compact, affordable system. Built using open-source software and economical hardware, EduBot delivers real-time interactive learning via a mobile application. Capabilities include voice-enabled Q&A, book scanning, storytelling, math problemsolving, and expressive gestures. Experimental results demonstrate EduBot’s superior performance: achieving OCR accuracies of 95.2% for Bangla and 97.6% for English, a response time of 150 ms, and significantly higher user satisfaction compared to existing solutions. Its modular architecture enables deployment across traditional, hybrid, and remote learning environments. Furthermore, its culturally relevant design ensures accessibility in resource-constrained settings. This work advances educational technology by offering a practical, scalable platform for personalized, AI-driven learning. EduBot establishes a new benchmark for low-cost, multilingual educational robots and presents a promising model for future integration into global learning ecosystems.
Notes: OSS is used to build the educational robot; the study evaluates its learning features and performance, not OSS project lifecycle or maintenance.

Author: S. C. R. Rijadi; E. Rohadi; N. Ambarsari; S. Suakanto; D. Pramesti; F. Hamami
Title: Development of Geographical Information System for Mangrove Monitoring (Case Study: Mangrove Malang Indonesia)
Abstract Note: Mangrove monitoring is crucial in Kabupaten Malang, a region known for its 18 beaches. The increasing trend of mangrove deforestation, driven by unchecked tourism activities, underscores the need for an effective monitoring system. There is limited oversight from the government, which exacerbates the issue. This study aims to develop a geographical information system for a mangrove monitoring website that provides valuable insights to stakeholders while promoting awareness about eco-tourism practices. The project adopts the prototyping methodology within the software development life cycle to facilitate effective communication between researchers and expert users from Kabupaten Malang. The website was developed using the Django stack, a robust web development framework. User acceptance testing employed the Blackbox method, with results indicating that the system meets all defined use cases. Specifically, six use cases for administrators and three for guests were successfully validated, demonstrating the website's readiness for implementation as a pilot proj ect in Kabupaten Malang. The evaluation phase highlights opportunities for future enhancements, such as incorporating additional user roles to improve privacy and access control, integrating the platform with government systems for broader adoption, and embedding tutorial pages for user guidance. Additionally, real-time data integration from external resources is suggested to improve monitoring capabilities and encourage eco-tourism. These improvements aim to strengthen mangrove monitoring efforts and boost tourist engagement by emphasizing sustainable tourism practices. This initiative offers a promising step toward balancing ecological preservation and tourism development in Kabupaten Malang.
Notes: The study develops a GIS website for mangrove monitoring; its population and subject are not OSS projects or ecosystems.

Author: M. R. Nechifor; A. Salceanu; M. V. Paulet
Title: Web-Application for Assisting Solar Storage Design
Abstract Note: The starting point of this paper is based on the need to design energy storage systems as correctly as possible, given that renewable energy sources, characterized by unpredictability and instability, will represent 57% of the world’s electricity production in the very next 10 years. Any large scale photovoltaic or wind power plant project must also contain a distinct part of a properly sized storage system. For the concrete case of Romania, are analyzed the seasonality index and practical potential (averaged over the entire surface of the country). These parameters influence the amount of electricity that can be produced by a certain photovoltaic plant within a year, including from the perspective of designing a system of adjacent storage. Then, for a certain geographical location, other four complementary parameters are customized and analyzed in detail. They all together provide essential information regarding the worst cases of solar illumination, for a certain number of consecutive days and for each month of the year. The calculation of these parameters was possible using the data made available by the open-source platform of the Power project supported by NASA. It is presented how to use this online tool, very functional for any calculation of electrical energy storage systems intended to ensure the autonomous operation of a photovoltaic plant not connected to the power grid. The results of the calculation of these four parameters associated with four representative locations in Romania are presented. These outputs can be displayed in graphical or tabular form. At the end there are presented considerations and comments regarding the interpretation, comparison and use of this data.
Notes: The study uses NASA’s open-source platform as a data tool to analyze solar-storage design; it does not study OSS project lifecycle or maintenance.

Author: K. Aktaş; O. İşleyen
Title: A Metric-Based Comparative Evaluation of Unit Test Quality Generated by AI Agents Under Different Prompting Schemes
Abstract Note: In recent years, advances in artificial intelligence have led companies to adopt AI agents to address challenges in software services such as uninterrupted and sustainable operation, rapid response times, and data management. These agents are used across a wide range of tasks, including code generation, error analysis, automation, and integration. However, their success largely depends on how they are guided. In other words, an AI agent produces outputs in line with the quality and specificity of the prompt it receives: well-designed prompts tend to yield more consistent and reliable results, whereas poorly designed prompts may lead to erroneous or inconsistent outputs. Since this effect is especially visible in software engineering artifacts that must be executable and correct, unit test generation provides a concrete and quantifiable setting to examine prompt impact. This study systematically evaluates the quality of unit tests generated by six state-of-the-art AI agents under five different prompting schemes. We assess test quality using three complementary metrics: code coverage, mutation testing and code maintainability. Our results indicate that structured prompting generally improves unit test quality, but the magnitude and consistency of these gains vary significantly by agent and metric, with occasional regressions under certain prompt settings. These findings provide actionable guidance for practitioners selecting AI agents and crafting prompts for automated unit test generation.
Notes: The study evaluates AI-generated unit-test quality and prompting schemes; it does not investigate OSS project lifecycle, abandonment, or a related maintenance outcome.

Author: A. Srivastava; A. Ahmad; S. Kumar; M. A. Ahmad
Title: Air Pollution Data and Forecasting Data Monitored through Google Cloud Services by using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
Abstract Note: The air to sustain life on Earth is a crucial ingredient. Consumption of fossil fuels, other nonrenewable energy sources, and environmental changes caused by industrial processes contribute significantly to the growth of air pollution. In order to maintain the health and success of all species living on Earth, the air quality must be continuously monitored. This work details the implementation and strategy of AI-based air pollution monitoring and forecasting based on Internet of Things (IoT). In addition, a web-based dashboard using Google's cloud platform and the ‘firebase’ API tracks air pollution levels in real-time, both here and now and in the future. The air's purity can find by some components like carbon monoxide (CO), ammonia (NH4), and ozone. These components are calculated by using different types of sensors. Sensors are placed in various places in Vijayawada's surroundings. To calculate the air pollution in respective areas, using other techniques based on the time series modelling process and by integrating the Auto regression model to the moving Average Model. In this process, input parameters are training data sets collected concerning time series. These input parameters are found by using innovative technology. Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) are two examples of performance indices used to verify the efficacy of different Time Series models (RMSE). Raspberry Pi-3 computer learning algorithm blinked. It is a node at the network's periphery. An online dashboard built on the open-source Google cloud firebase tracks air pollution readings and predictions for the next four hours.
Notes: The study concerns air-pollution monitoring and forecasting; open-source Firebase is only a platform, with no OSS project lifecycle or maintenance topic.

Author: C. Vinoth Kumar; P. Selvaprabhu; N. Baska; U. Vivek Menon; V. Babu Kumaravelu; S. Chinnadurai; F. Ali
Title: Ethereum Blockchain Framework Enabling Banks to Know Their Customers
Abstract Note: The Know Your Customer (KYC) process is a fundamental prerequisite for any financial institution’s compliance with the regulatory framework. Blockchain technology has emerged as a revolutionary solution to enhance the effectiveness of the KYC procedure. It ensures that the KYC process is transparent, secure, and immutable, thereby offering a robust solution to combat fraudulent activities. The potential of blockchain technology in revolutionizing the KYC process has been acknowledged globally. Blockchain technology provides a decentralized platform for storing customer data, enabling financial institutions to access the information seamlessly. Using ethereum blockchain technology in KYC procedures can enhance the efficiency of financial institutions, significantly reducing the time and cost associated with the process. This work aims to provide a viable and sustainable solution to the challenges that banks experience in implementing KYC procedures and onboarding new customers. The proposed solution involves the central bank maintaining a comprehensive register of all registered banks while closely monitoring their adherence to the existing regulations governing KYC and customer acquisition.
Notes: The study proposes an Ethereum-based KYC solution for banks; OSS project lifecycle, maintenance, or abandonment is not investigated.
